News.title: Man in his 20s dies after entering canal in police chase during Notting Hill Carnival
News.content:
CARNIVAL TRAGEDY Man in his 20s dies after entering canal in police chase during Notting Hill Carnival

A MAN in his 20s has died after entering a canal while being pursued by police during Notting Hill Carnival.

Cops tried to stop the man at 3.19pm on Monday as he approached the carnival area in west London.

The man fled on foot and went into the canal near Meanwhile Gardens, according to the Metropolitan Police.

Officers and members of the public frantically sprung into action and managed to pull him from the water.





CPR was carried out and he was rushed to a central London hospital.

Despite the very best efforts of all involved, he was pronounced dead a short time later just before 4.45pm.

Urgent enquiries are now ongoing to locate and inform his next of kin.

Commander Claire Smart said: “This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the man who has lost his life.

“Any death following contact with the police is passed to the Independent Office for Police Conduct so the circumstances can be fully investigated. I would encourage everyone to avoid speculation while this work takes place.

“I acknowledge the efforts of the officers and members of the public who entered the canal to rescue this man.

“I know they will be devastated that his life couldn’t ultimately be saved.”

Cops arrested 351 people on Notting Hill Carnival’s final day as the party came to a close on Monday after millions flocked to the streets.



The arrests were related to several offences including possession of a handgun and sexual offender licence breaches.

This brings the total number of arrests over the celebration to 560.

But while officers responded to a number of incidents, they said “the mood has been overwhelmingly positive and celebratory”.

The annual west London carnival is Europe’s biggest street party and billed by organisers as “the greatest community-led event on the planet”.

The carnival includes parades, live music, street food and sound stages and is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year.



Commander Smart of the Met Police said: “This is the second year now that we have seen a marked difference in the prevalence of serious violence at carnival.

“This is the result of not just proactive policing and a determined effort to target our efforts on those posing the greatest risk of harm, but of a collaborative partnership approach to the delivery of the whole event.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The progress by Notting Hill Carnival Ltd in stepping into so many of the event management and crowd safety roles previously performed by the police cannot be understated.

“They have delivered a challenging event well and in doing so have allowed us to focus our resources on our core role of tackling crime.”

News.title: M25 closed after serious crash as drivers issued Heathrow and Gatwick Airport warning
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAFFIC CHAOS M25 closed after serious crash as drivers issued Heathrow and Gatwick Airport warning

A MAJOR UK motorway has been closed after a serious crash with drivers heading to Heathrow and Gatwick Airport facing huge delays.

The M25 is shut in Surrey between J10, Wisley and J11, Chertsey following the crash at 11.55pm yesterday night.

Surrey Police are on scene and have warned drivers travelling to Heathrow and Gatwick Airport to allow extra travel time as delays are expected.

Motorists have been advised to use diversion routes.





Drivers have also been told to avoid the M25 Junction 10 – Junction 11 as traffic queues are expected.

Emergency services are in attendance and traffic cameras show queues of vehicles on the road.

The road will be closed for a number of hours to allow a thorough investigation to take place.

National Highways Traffic Officers are in attendance assisting with traffic management.

The A245 (Parvis Road) is also closed in both directions.

The northbound carriageway between J10 towards J11 has since been reopened but delays still remain.

Traffic is building on the M25 as rush hour gets underway with cars stuck bumper-to-bumper in heavy traffic.

National Highways warned drivers to allow extra time for travel.



A spokesperson said: “If this impacts on your planned route, please allow extra journey time.”

The force said in a statement earlier: “The M25 is currently closed both ways between J10, Wisley and J11, Chertsey due to a serious collision.

“If travelling to Heathrow Airport or Gatwick Airport, please check your travel time before you depart as your journey is likely to be impacted.”

News.title: Man, 23, charged with murder over house fire that killed girl, 7, and her aunt in Middlesbrough
News.content:
BLAZE 'MURDER' Man, 23, charged with murder over house fire that killed girl, 7, and her aunt in Middlesbrough

A MAN has been charged with murder after a seven-year-old girl and her aunt were killed in a house fire in Middlesbrough.

Young Valentina Foster and Natalie McDonald, 34, tragically died in the blaze at 5.23am on Wednesday.



Valentina had tragically begged relatives to let her spend the night to help celebrate Natalie’s daughter’s 15th birthday.

Her distraught gran Valerie Foster, seen hugging the youngster in a family photo, said: “Life is so cruel. My beautiful granddaughter, Valentina.”



A 23-year-old man has been charged with two counts of murder, two counts of Section 18 GBH with intent, and two counts of attempted section 18 GBH with intent.

He will appear at Teesside Magistrates’ Court today.



Senior Investigating Officer, Katie Smith from Northumbria Police, said: “This has been a truly tragic incident, and my thoughts remain with the families of all those involved.

“I would like to thank local residents for their support and patience during this complex investigation.



“Anyone who may still have information, or has any concerns, can still submit Information using the Major Incident Public Portal.”

Katie Nicolson, Chief Crown Prosecutor for CPS North East, added: “Our prosecutors have worked closely with Cleveland Police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court.

“We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial.

“It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings.”

Detectives are not linking the blaze to the crash on the A66 last weekend, Cleveland Police have said.



Seven people, including two police officers, were killed in the horror – sparking a wave of violence in Middlesbrough.

Assistant Chief Constable Dave Sutherland said previously: “Since the tragic incident last Saturday morning in which seven people sadly lost their lives… officers and staff have remained working around the clock to continue to serve the public of Cleveland.

“In the same week, we have also seen a tragic house fire on Wednesday in which two people lost their lives, which is also understandably impacting the force and our local communities.



“At this time, we are not linking this incident to the fatal collision on the A66.

“Our thoughts remain with all those affected by these incidents as we continue our investigations into what happened.”

A woman, 48 was pulled from the fire and taken to hospital in Newcastle upon Tyne in a critical condition.

Three others were hurt, including one who jumped from an upstairs window.

Their injuries are not said to be life-threatening.



Aerial images showed the house’s charred roof beams and blackened windows as cops fought to contain the street violence.

Witness Ellie, 20, who declined to give her surname, said: “I could hear kids screaming and was shouting for people to help. The house was scorching.

“I couldn’t get near the front it was that hot. Two kids got out from upstairs.”

Ellie stayed with the woman who leapt to safety from upstairs.

She added: “She was crying, in pain and in a bad way.”



Another witness who did not wish to be named said: “I saw the girl being carried by a firefighter.”

The families of those involved are being supported by family liaison officers.

On Wednesday, Valentina’s uncle Dean Foster wrote: “Such a beautiful baby girl. Life can be so cruel.”

Relative Sarah Harland-Foster added: “Why, why, why? All I keep telling myself.

“My heart’s absolutely torn to bits. Back in the arms of your dad my beautiful girl.”



Billie-Jo Foster said: “Aw my Valentina. How? Why you? You’re just a baby.”

Meanwhile, Natalie’s mum Lisa Kirton told the BBC that Valentina, known as Tina, had been staying with the family over the school holidays.

She said Natalie “had a heart of gold who would give anyone anything. We’re still in the hospital with the daughter. “

The 15-year-old and her friend “kicked out a window” and jumped to safety, Lisa said.

She continued: “Her father died two years ago so this child is not in a good way.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking to The Times, Lisa added: “Natalie’s husband is in intensive care and has been put in an induced coma.

“There is speculation that the fire was caused on purpose but I don’t really know much about what happened.”

News.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis found guilty of murdering rap legend Tupac Shakur in 1996 hit
News.content:
A VERDICT has been reached in the long-awaited trial of the only man ever charged over the murder of rap legend Tupac Shakur.

Duane “Keffe D” Davis, 63, was found guilty of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon nearly three decades after the star was gunned down.



The decision was handed down at Clark County District Court in Las Vegas, bringing one of the most notorious unsolved killings in music history closer to a conclusion.

He was found guilty of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote or assist a criminal gang.



Davis had pleaded not guilty and denied having any role in the September 1996 drive-by shooting.

He was accused of helping organize the revenge attack after Shakur and members of his entourage beat Davis’ nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, inside the MGM Grand earlier that night.



Prosecutors never alleged that Davis himself pulled the trigger.

Instead, they argued the former South Side Compton Crips leader helped set the killing in motion and supplied the gun used in the attack.

Under Nevada law, someone who aids or helps arrange a murder can be held responsible even if they did not fire the fatal shots.

Shakur, 25, was riding in a black BMW driven by Death Row Records boss Marion “Suge” Knight on September 7, 1996, when a white Cadillac pulled up alongside them near the Las Vegas Strip.



Gunfire erupted, leaving Shakur critically wounded and Knight injured.

The California Love rapper died in hospital six days later on September 13.

The killing stunned the music world and became one of hip-hop’s most enduring mysteries.

No one was charged for nearly 27 years.

The case eventually zeroed in on Davis after he repeatedly discussed the shooting in interviews, conversations with investigators and his 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend.



Jurors were played hours of recordings in which Davis described being inside the Cadillac on the night Shakur was shot.

In his earlier accounts, Davis said he and three other men went looking for Shakur and Knight after Anderson was beaten.

He said he obtained a gun and passed it toward the back of the Cadillac before shots were fired into Shakur’s BMW.



Davis previously named his nephew Anderson as the gunman, although other accounts have pointed to another passenger, Deandrae Smith.

Prosecutors did not ask jurors to decide who actually fired the weapon.

The other three men Davis said were inside the Cadillac have all since died, leaving him as the only surviving alleged occupant.

Prosecutors argued Davis’ descriptions of the shooting remained consistent on the crucial points and matched information investigators had developed about the case.

But defense attorney Michael Sanft told jurors his client had spent years exaggerating and telling sensational stories for attention and money.



The defense argued there was no physical evidence establishing Davis was even inside the Cadillac when Shakur was killed.

Davis did not testify in his own defense.

His lawyers instead called former investigators in an effort to show that key parts of his earlier accounts could never be independently confirmed.



Retired Las Vegas homicide detective Dan Long told jurors he had tried to verify details Davis gave police during an interview years after the killing.

“I wasn’t able to verify any of that,” Long testified.

Long said he could not independently establish that Davis had been inside the Cadillac and was unable to find records supporting some other parts of his story.

But prosecutors pointed out that Davis had identified the same four alleged occupants of the car that investigators had already focused on.

Long also testified that he believed there had been enough probable cause to seek an arrest warrant after interviewing Davis, although prosecutors at the time told investigators to hold off while the case was reviewed.



The trial also saw dramatic testimony from former Mob Piru member James “Mob James” McDonald, who openly told the courtroom he did not want his answers to help send Davis to prison.

“You’re asking me something that wouldn’t be good for [Davis],” McDonald told the defense during one tense exchange.

Jurors ultimately heard 24 prosecution witnesses and three defense witnesses across nine days of evidence before the case headed to closing arguments.

Prosecutors urged the panel to trust Davis’ own words, arguing his years of public comments had effectively placed him at the heart of the revenge plot.



The defense maintained those same statements could not be treated as a reliable confession when investigators lacked hard evidence to back them up.

Davis was arrested and indicted in September 2023, reviving a case that had remained without a prosecution for almost three decades.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Shakur’s relatives attended the trial, which unfolded just weeks before the 30th anniversary of his death.

The rapper remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop, with his killing continuing to fuel questions, investigations and theories for decades.

News.title: Brit, 31, stabbed to death at railway station in Germany named as popular pub landlady
News.content:
BRUTAL ATTACK Brit, 31, stabbed to death at railway station in Germany named as popular pub landlady

A BRITISH woman stabbed to death at a railway station in Germany was named as a popular pub landlady as tributes were paid yesterday.

The 31-year-old woman died of wounds suffered in a mystery knife attack in Rosenheim, Bavaria at 12.50 am on Sunday.



Bavarian police said she died in hospital of “severe” injuries and arrested a 27-year-old German man near the scene immediately after the horror.

The man appeared in court yesterday and was ordered to be taken to a secure psychiatric hospital as police probed the motive for the attack.



Social media posts paid tributes and named a woman described as a Buckinghamshire pub landlady, though Foreign Office officials have yet to confirm relatives have been informed.

But a friend posted on Facebook: “She (not mentioning her name out of respect to her family) was our local landlady who was on her way to support a friend at a funeral in Austria.

“This lady was an old soul and everyone in our local always felt safe and secure, and she turned the local around to modernise it but also keep it a welcoming safe space for our community.

“A true professional in hospitality with grace and dignity.

“She loved her dog so much and was so tolerant and non judgemental.

“We are absolutely devastated for her loss and for the loss her family. Her beautiful dog who was our dog’s best friend.



“Our whole community know and are processing slowly in shock and are in mourning.”

Police revealed the knifeman was a German citizen of no fixed address.

The attractive pub boss was also a keen runner who ran the 2022 London Marathon to raise money for the Spinal Injuries Association and finished gruelling Iron Man events.

Locals said she had turned around her historic 17th century pub, transforming the run-down boozer into a thriving community hub after modernisation work.

Another friend posted: “The lady was so lovely – knew her very well.



“Just can’t believe it, Only saw her Saturday lunchtime and then 12 hours later she (bless her) is no longer with us….”

Rosenheim is one of the largest cities in Upper Bavaria acting as a rail hub for passengers travelling to Austrian cities including Vienna, Salzburg and Innsbruck.

The Rosenheimer Herbstfest – an event similar to the Oktoberfest beer festival – is currently taking place in the area.

Rosenheim Mayor Abuzar Erdogan said “there are no indications of a security threat in our city or of any link to our Herbstfest”.

“The criminal investigation department is working closely with the public prosecutor’s office to investigate the circumstances.”



A Foreign Office spokesman said: “We are supporting the family of a British woman who died in Germany [and] are in touch with the local authorities.”

News.title: Fury as major historic English cities could LOSE their prized status due to Rayner’s barmy local government reforms
News.content:
HISTORIC cities across England could lose their prized status because of Angela Rayner’s barmy local government reforms.

Winchester and even Canterbury have held city status by ancient prescriptive right for at least 837 predating English common law.



But plans stirred up by the Secretary for Housing, Communities and Local Government two-tier county and district councils are being abolished.

It means cities face being merged into unitary authorities, which require a new charter trustee to continue to use the city’s title and coat and arms.



Cities that fail to do this will lose their status.

Ancient Roman settlement Winchester – which served as the capital of England during Anglo-Saxon rule – risks being consumed by the creation of Mid Hampshire council.

Meanwhile, Canterbury – whose city council and mayor date from 1448 during Henry VI’s reign – risks being earmarked to become part of the East Kent authority.

Stoke-on-Trent, Chelmsford and Southend-on-Sea could also be affected.

Gareth Bacon, the shadow local government minister, said: “This is Labour’s constitutional wrecking ball.”

News.title: Teen, 16, set for court in Tyrone charged with murder of man, 61, two counts of attempted murder & threats to kill
News.content:
MURDER RAP Teen, 16, set for court in Tyrone charged with murder of man, 61, two counts of attempted murder & threats to kill

A 16-year old boy is set to appear in court charged with murder, two counts of attempted murder and threats to kill following the death of a 61-year-old man at a home in Co Tyrone.

The deceased’s wife and eight-year-old daughter were also found injured at the house in the Lisnahull Road area of Dungannon on Saturday.

Emergency services were dispatched to the scene at 10.55am on August 29 after police received a report of an ongoing “disturbance”.

The 61-year-old man was found deceased at the scene.





He was from Guinea-Bissau but had been living and working in the area for over 20 years.

His 48-year-old wife “had sustained non-life threatening injuries” but the couple’s daughter had been “severely injured”.

Both mother and daughter were airlifted to hospital and the girl’s condition remained “critical” over the weekend.

However, the PSNI confirmed this afternoon that the eight-year-old is now “stable” and her mother was discharged from hospital over the weekend.



Detectives from the Police Service of Northern Ireland’s Major Investigation Team said the teenager is due to appear before Omagh Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, September 1.

The 16-year-old is charged with murder, two counts of attempted murder and threats to kill.

A spokesperson for the force said: “Detectives from the Police Service of Northern Ireland’s Major Investigation Team have charged a 16-year-old male to court following the death of a man in the Lisnahull Road area of Dungannon on Saturday, 29th August.

“The teenager is charged with murder, two counts of attempted murder and threats to kill.



“He is due to appear before Omagh Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, 1st September.

“As is usual procedure, all charges will be reviewed by the Public Prosecution Service.”

News.title: Moment biker zooming down road crashes INSIDE open doors of bus before climbing back out
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a motorbike slams into a bus – but its open doors let the rider land safely inside.

Shocking footage shows how a bus’ open doors save the biker’s life.



The motorbike rider can be seen slamming into the bus at high speed at a junction in Buga, Colombia.

His bike is thrown in the air with the force of the crash.



It slams to the ground, with pieces breaking off at it does so.

But because the bus’s doors were open, the bike’s rider lands inside the bus.

CCTV from inside the vehicle shows the dramatic moment the biker flies into the bus.

He is flipped upside down, bouncing on his head on a seat.



The force breaks part of the bus door.

Miraculously, the rider remains conscious and can climb back out of the bus.

Just one passenger is seen inside the bus and the biker does not hit anyone else on his way in.



The driver stops the bus and the rider gets to his feet, seeming to escape without serious injury.

He was hospitalised to rule out any internal injuries, Infobae reported.

The terrifying crash took place at the crossing between seventh Street and 13th Avenue on Sunday.

The motorcyclist allegedly went through a red light before colliding with the bus.

It comes after a teen singer who starred on The Voice Kids was struck by a hit-and-run driver who fled the scene in Quindio, Colombia earlier this year.



Nicole Valeria Vargas Gomez, 19, died in the horror crash.

She appeared on Colombia’s edition of The Voice Kids in 2019 at just 12 years old.

William Andres Paipa, 40, also died in the collision on the Circasia–Armenia road in western Colombia.

Cops said the pair were crossing the road when an unidentified vehicle smashed into them out of nowhere.

News.title: Ex-gang boss found guilty in 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur
News.content:
Prosecutors had argued during the trial that although Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips street gang, did not fire the gun that killed Shakur, he ordered the shooting and supplied the gun that his nephew Orlando Anderson used to open fire.

They told the court that Davis had planned the shooting as retaliation after Anderson was involved in a fight with Shakur and the rapper's crew in Las Vegas just hours earlier.

For 30 years, the case remained one of America's most famous cold cases, spurring countless conspiracies - but never a conviction, until now.

Shakur's murder happened at a time of intense rivalry between the East Coast and West Coast rap scene and amid gang feuds between the Bloods and Crips, which had deep roots within hip-hop at the time.

His family appeared emotional in court, his sister embracing a prosecutor after the verdict was read while others sat crying nearby.

Outside, devoted fans of Shakur were crying and cheering.

The key evidence in the case were Davis' own words, where he repeatedly and publicly acknowledged being inside the white Cadillac from where the deadly shots were fired.

He had told authorities about his role in Shakur's death during a secret 2008 police interview related to the death of fellow rapper Notorious B.I.G., real name Christopher Wallace.

Davis elaborated further on his role in his 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend.

But his book and media interviews voided a protective agreement he had established with authorities that had blocked any criminal charges being filed, with the court ruling his police interview could be used in the murder trial against him.

In closing arguments, prosecutor Binu Palal told jurors to take Davis at his word and find him guilty.

For years, he argued, Davis had been telling people "that he is responsible for Tupac Shakur's murder" through documentaries, his memoir, podcasts and a police interview.

"He's the shot caller - in every instance in every iteration he's the leader of the South Side Crips," Palal told the jury.

"When you have the shot caller sitting shotgun when shots are fired, there's no doubt he's responsible."

News.title: More cells being built within prisons to help tackle overcrowding
News.content:
The government is spending Â£110m on creating more cells in existing prisons in England and Wales as part of its plans to tackle overcrowding.

The money, which has been "fast-tracked from existing budgets", will be used to speed up the construction of hundreds of new prison places, the Ministry of Justice has said.

Existing space within prisons, such as unused office space, laundry rooms and storage areas, will be converted into cells.

The announcement comes at a time of crisis for the prison system, which is close to maximum capacity, with the government being criticised for its handling of an early release scheme.

Lord Chancellor and Justice Secretary Alex Norris said the government would be "getting spades in the ground quicker to deliver thousands more places to lock up dangerous criminals and keep the public safe".

Norris said: "This government is serious about fixing the broken prison system we inherited, which is why we've already delivered more than 3,200 prison places in just two years.

"We're now investing to boost these efforts further."

Investment to create more prison spaces was announced as part of the government's 2025 spending review, which covered plans for the period from 2024â25 to 2029â30.

As part of this, it allocated a Â£7bn capital investment to create 14,000 prison places by 2031.

The Â£110m announced on Monday is not a new investment, and is being drawn from money previously announced.

The Lord Chancellor will update Parliament on Tuesday, setting out changes to upcoming sentencing reforms which will block hundreds more dangerous offenders from earlier release.

Measures also include plans to remove foreign national offenders more quickly, and ending the historic injustice of Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences in a way that balances fairness and public safety, the government has said.

Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said: "It is absurd for Labour to talk about a 'prison building boom' when there are 700 fewer prison places than a year ago.

"In a matter of weeks thousands of dangerous criminals will be released onto our streets thanks to Andy Burnham, including perpetrators of some of the most vile crimes."

An extra Â£18.9m investment into vital services for victims will also be announced to Parliament.

The services will provide the specialist emotional and practical support needed to help victims move on with their lives, according to the Ministry of Justice (MoJ).

This money will be reprioritised from existing budgets and will be on top of the Â£550m already announced by government for this support.

The MoJ also announced that it had signed a contract to start building a new jail for 1,700 hundred inmates in Lancashire.

News.title: Burnham to promise 'sense of optimism' in first Commons statement as PM
News.content:
The Conservatives and Reform UK, however, are preparing to attack his policies, questioning how they will be funded and whether there will be new tax rises.

Kemi Badenoch reshuffled her shadow cabinet team on Monday in preparation for this moment. To sharpen her party's attacks on Labour over its handling of tax and the economy she promoted Andrew Griffith to be her new shadow chancellor.

The Conservatives are making much of his past jobs in business. Before entering politics he was chief financial officer and chief operating officer at Sky, and chair of Just Eat.

He is promising a Conservative government that would deliver "lower, simpler taxes, get Britain drilling again to bring down energy costs, slash the red tape holding Britain back, and scrap the job-killing measures in Labour's (Un)Employment Rights Act".

Labour and the Liberal Democrats have seized on the fact Griffith was a Treasury minister in Liz Truss's government and publicly defended her "mini-budget".

Bridget Phillipson, the Labour Party chair, said the "Tories' top team is crammed full of the same vandals who hammered family finances and left our public services crumbling".

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said Griffith's appointment showed the Conservatives were "happy to forfeit any claim to economic credibility".

Burnham will face criticism from the Greens too. Their leader, Zack Polanski, says that Burnham's ideas for greater public control over vital services is "just tinkering".

Polanski says "if he really wants to bring back hope, he needs to tax the wealthy, take water and energy back under public ownership, bring in rent controls, and say no to new North Sea drilling".

The Liberal Democrats are already attacking Burnham's plans to deal with the prisons crisis.

Their justice spokesperson, Jess Brown-Fuller, said Labour's promise to build new cells was not backed by any new money and proved "just how unserious this Government remains about fixing our justice system".

Other major challenges facing Burnham include defence. How will he fund the plans he has inherited from Sir Keir? And, beyond that, how fast will he increase spending to meet Nato commitments?

There are imminent decisions to be made about whether to approve new drilling for oil and gas in the North Sea. There are looming choices about whether to do more to help as energy bills rise this winter, whether to increase taxes at the Budget. And longer-term issues about reforms to welfare, social care and ties with the EU.

All of which means that the moment when Burnham rises to address MPs on Tuesday may well be the point when his honeymoon period as prime minister ends and the hard work begins.

News.title: New storm names for 2026-2027 released by Met Office
News.content:
Storm names are selected jointly by the Met Office, Met Ãireann and KNMI, with the final list aiming to reflect communities across the UK, Ireland and the Netherlands.

In 2025 the three meteorology agencies invited nominations for names from the public.

More than 40,000 were submitted - we saw names such as Amy, Isla and Marty selected for the 2025/2026 storm season.

This year's list continues to draw on those suggestions, reflecting not only popular choices, but also some of the personal stories behind them.

For example Austen was suggested in honour of Austen Nagle, the first director of the Irish Meteorological Service.

Chloe was selected by the Met Office after being nominated more than 130 times, including once by the mother of a five-year-old who is described by her mum as "fascinated by the weather" but can also "create a storm by herself" when she is tired.

And Ivy was nominated in honour of a nine-month-old Labrador puppy affectionately known as "the absolute destructor".

Any remnant of a tropical storm or hurricane that crosses the Atlantic will keep its original name, for example ex-Hurricane Erin, which brought a large swell to South West England in August 2025 and was named 'Storm Erin'.

To ensure consistency with the US National Hurricane Centre naming conventions, names that begin with the letters Q, U, X, Y and Z are not used.

News.title: New super flu vaccine rollout begins as NHS regroups from 'busiest summer'
News.content:
Last winter's flu season was unexpected, beginning more than a month earlier than usual, external with the Super-K strain.

Super flu is not a medical term, and it does not mean the virus has become harder to treat, just that people are yet to build up immunity against it.

Flu vaccines are updated annually to ensure they are a good match for the type of flu circulating. Influenza viruses constantly mutate and experts have to predict these changes ahead of time.

This year's vaccine has had a few tweaks, including one to better match subclade K.

It is not clear when flu will hit this year, and whether it will be a bad season. But experts often look to southern hemisphere countries, like Australia and New Zealand, to gain a better understanding of how the UK could be affected.

Their flu season peaks in July or August, and these countries have so far had a relatively mild year in terms of cases.

Dr Amanda Doyle from NHS England said it was best to be cautious.

"Last year's flu season came early and was made worse by a new variant, which had a major impact for patients and put enormous pressure on urgent and emergency care services across the country," she said.

"With the NHS experiencing its busiest summer on record, staff have started preparing for this winter earlier than ever â and with services already under significant pressure, it is vital that everyone offered the vaccine comes forward."

News.title: Hundreds remember Heaton Park synagogue attack victims at memorial event
News.content:
The Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis and Communities Secretary Angela Rayner were among about 800 people who attended a memorial event for the victims and survivors of last year's Heaton Park synagogue attack.

Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed, and three others injured, as they tried to defend their place of worship from attacker Jihad al-Shamie on 2 October 2025.

Relatives of the bereaved and some of the survivors were among the speakers at Monday's service of remembrance at the synagogue in Manchester.

Prior to the event, Rabbi Daniel Walker said the Jewish community feels less safe now than it did immediately after the attack.

He said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation â and British Jews more widely â feeling increasingly vulnerable.

Two seats remained empty for the service, bearing the names of Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby.

News.title: Orangutans in danger as wildfires blaze through Borneo
News.content:
A weak orangutan was found laying on the ground in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Borneo island.

Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze from wildfires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra islands.

The wildfires have destroyed part of the habitat of hundreds of orangutans and risking the survival of the species.

"The situation is quite critical", said Karmele Llano Sanchez, CEO of the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI).

Sanchez said the fires are "leaving [the orangutans] without any food or water".

The orangutan found will be moved to a rehabilitation centre to get more treatment and will be released back into the wild after recovery, according to YIARI.

News.title: Summer 2026 expected to be declared UK's hottest on record
News.content:
There is something striking about the way the UK's summer temperature record is being broken.

In a climate that isn't changing, new records should generally become progressively rarer, because every time a record falls, it raises the bar for the next one.

Instead, all five of the UK's hottest summers on record have occurred since 2000, external. And until last year, the margins between them were tiny: the four hottest were separated by just five hundredths of a degree.

Then came 2025. The record jumped by 0.34C. Now, just a year later, it looks like that record has gone too.

"Record-shattering" sounds like the kind of language we journalists would use. In fact, it is a term climate scientists use for records broken by unusually large margins. Research suggests, external these big jumps become more likely if the climate is warming rapidly.

So why is this happening so quickly here? The UK sits on the western edge of Europe, the fastest-warming continent on Earth - warming at roughly twice the global rate.

There are a few reasons for that. Land heats up faster than the oceans, parts of Europe stretch into the rapidly warming Arctic, and changes in weather patterns have favoured more frequent and intense summer heatwaves.

Scientists are still working out exactly how much each factor contributes, but the result is clear: the background climate in which British weather happens is getting warmer.

None of this means the UK will break its summer record every year. Weather will always give us cooler summers as well as hotter ones. But the pattern is becoming unmistakable: records that once marked the extreme edge of the UK's climate are being overtaken with remarkable speed.

So the question is not whether the UK will experience summers hotter than this one. It is how often they will come - and how much hotter they might be.

News.title: Boy, 16, charged with murder and attempted murder
News.content:
A 16-year-old boy has been charged with the murder of a man in Dungannon, County Tyrone, and the attempted murder of two other people in the same incident.

The body of the dead man, who was 61, was found alongside his injured eight-year-old daughter at a house on Lisnahull Road on Saturday morning,

The man's 48-year-old wife sustained non-life threatening injuries during the attack.

The teenage boy, who has also been charged with making threats to kill, is due to appear before Omagh Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

News.title: Man dies near Notting Hill Carnival after entering canal
News.content:
A man died near Notting Hill Carnival in London on Monday afternoon, the Metropolitan Police have confirmed.

Police officers had attempted to stop the man, believed to be in his 20s, as he approached the event. He fled on foot with officers in pursuit, and entered the water in the vicinity of Meanwhile Gardens a short time later, the force said.

Taken to hospital by ambulance the man was pronounced dead a short time later.

Cdr Claire Smart said: "This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the man who has lost his life."

The Met Police said officers had attempted to stop the man at about 15:19 BST near Harrow Road.

The man entered the water in the vicinity of Meanwhile Gardens, off Kensal Road.

Officers and members of the public went in after him and pulled him from the water, police said, and officers immediately started CPR.

Paramedics were called and continued treatment at the canal side before taking the man to a central London hospital. He was pronounced dead at 16:43.

The Met Police said on Monday night that urgent enquiries were ongoing to locate and inform his next of kin.

Smart, gold commander for the Notting Hill Festival, said: "Any death following contact with the police is passed to the Independent Office for Police Conduct so the circumstances can be fully investigated.

"I would encourage everyone to avoid speculation while this work takes place."

She added: "I acknowledge the efforts of the officers and members of the public who entered the canal to rescue this man. I know they will be devastated that his life couldn't ultimately be saved."

The Met Police said the two days of the festival had passed "largely without incident".

There were two assaults with knives - one stabbing and one slashing. Neither resulted in life-threatening injuries.

On Monday evening, police said there had been 315 arrests that day, bringing the total number of arrests to 560.

News.title: Holy Cross school dispute was 'hatred at its worst'
News.content:
The priest who helped shield schoolgirls during the 2001 Holy Cross dispute has said the "hurt" of that ordeal could happen again.

Speaking on the 25th anniversary of Holy Cross, Fr Aidan Troy said that possibility is what keeps him "devoted to dialogue, to conversation, to searching for justice and to caring about people".

Fr Aidan said the sectarian dispute was "hatred at its worst".

It happened in north Belfast when loyalist protesters tried to block the route taken by Holy Cross school pupils and their parents, who were from a Catholic background, on their walk to class.

Following the initial violence, the police and Army put up crash barriers to keep a corridor route open for the Holy Cross pupils.

The images of terrified schoolgirls having to run the gauntlet between lines of armoured police officers in order to get to their primary school were beamed around the world.

Protestants claimed that Catholics were attacking their homes and said the school protest was their way of highlighting their concerns.

Stones, bottles, fireworks and even a blast bomb were thrown during weeks of unrest.

Fr Aidan, who was parish priest in Ardoyne at the time, told BBC News NI that "none of us want to see hatred".

News.title: AI could cause global economic downturn, Andrew Bailey warns G20
News.content:
The governor of the Bank of England has warned G20 finance ministers that artificial intelligence could cause a global economic downturn and pose a significant cyber security risk to financial systems.

Andrew Bailey said any collapse of growth in the AI sector could lead to a "future market correction" that spreads worldwide.

In an open letter to finance ministers in the US on Monday, he said companies around the world should prepare for security breaches "involving simultaneous disruption across multiple firms".

Earlier this month, a group of 100 firms, including Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI, urged countries and groups to beef up their cyber defences before AI grows powerful enough to override them.

Bailey told the G20 finance ministers that a combination of highly priced stock markets, increased borrowing by investors, and the growing concentration of money into a small number of major technology companies could amplify any future market correction.

"The issue is not simply that investors are borrowing more, but that leverage is interacting with high valuations and market concentration, in particular the increasing cross-investment between artificial intelligence (AI) companies and hyper scalers, in a way that could amplify a future market correction," he said.

Bailey has called on those in charge of financial security to develop "appropriate steps to support safe and responsible model release and deployment on a global basis".

Bailey, who was writing in his capacity as chairman of the Financial Stability Board international watchdog (FSB), expressed concern about the "volatility" prompted by the effect of energy supply shocks caused by the US-Iran war.

His warning comes several months after UK Chancellor John Healey announced a Â£100m fund aimed at backing British AI start-ups.

That is part of the government's efforts to grow the country's "sovereign AI" capacity, developing homegrown AI technology to ensure the UK is not dependent on services from abroad.

Ministers want to see companies compete for the funding to help tackle challenges like cutting waiting lists in the NHS and bolstering cybersecurity and defence.

A UK government spokesperson said its new AI economics institute was working with international partners to build "a stronger shared understanding of how AI is transforming economies around the world."

"The institute is the first government-backed body of its kind focused on AI's economic impact, helping policymakers understand what AI means for growth, productivity, jobs and public services as the technology develops at pace," the spokesperson said.

But there is growing concern that AI companies are increasingly developing models that can easily override the safeguarding systems of banks and financial centres.

News.title: Nursery fined after baby boy burned by bleach
News.content:
Defence advocate Barry Smith KC said the first priority of a nursery was the safety and wellbeing of the children there.

He added: "It is of the utmost regret from all involved - from the director and all staff - that this accident occurred and injury was caused to a young child."

In a statement released via law firm Digby Brown, the family said: "We've had to wait five years for Little Dreams Nursery to admit what happened to our son was their fault but we don't feel the severity of his injuries have been acknowledged.

"We trusted them to take care of him and for such an injury to happen to a 10-month-old baby is indefensible.

"In the months and years that followed, we had to watch our boy deal with the consequences of something that was never his fault. No parent should have to experience that, but we are thankful what happened hasn't had a more serious or longer-lasting impact."

The statement concluded: "Today we close the most horrific chapter of our lives and we want to thank everyone who has supported us during this time and now request our privacy as we move forward."

Little Dreams said the safety, wellbeing and care of every child entrusted to them was of the "highest priority".

"We deeply regret that this incident was able to occur and are profoundly sorry for the distress and impact it has had on the child and their family," the nursery said.

News.title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems
News.content:
Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.

Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.

The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.

The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".

The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.

Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.

More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.

Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.

The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.

"We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.

Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.

The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.

This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).

"After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.

"The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.

"That means fully funding the pay award and properly funding all our schools and colleges to stem the recruitment and retention crisis and give children the education they deserve."

"As Lucy Powell enters her first term as education secretary the Liberal Democrats are calling for her first act to be to introduce an emergency package of 'back to school' measures to face this crisis head on," Voaden said.

The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.

Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.

The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.

The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.

An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.

"Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.

"We're taking action by announcing pay awards of almost 17% over two years, funding schools to improve maternity pay and offering targeted support to normalise flexible working and manageable workloads so that more teachers stay in our classrooms and thrive."

News.title: Business groups urge Swinney to scrap 'ineffective' food price cap plan
News.content:
The SRC said the policy also risked forcing small shops which are not covered by the proposed legislation to be uncompetitive.

"Scottish consumers benefit from the most affordable food prices in western Europe," MacDonald-Russell added.

"We know food price inflation is a problem, but the best model to deal with it is the one we have right now and price caps are going to make that worse.

"It is giving a false promise that it is going to be able to help with something.

"In reality, there is as good a chance it is going to make the overall cost of a shopping basket higher, because the cost of the scheme as well as the cap have to be absorbed by businesses."

It is thought the proposals would require changes to the UK Internal Markets Act of 2020, which was brought in after Brexit to prevent trade barriers and regulatory divergence between England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland as powers returned from the EU.

The Scottish government said helping people with the cost of living was a "top priority".

A spokesperson added: "Ministers have welcomed engagement with stakeholders, including retailers, food producers and farmers on proposals for food price controls.

"A consultation will launch shortly for further views."

News.title: Transfer deadline day LIVE: Julian Alvarez to Arsenal latest, Enzo Fernandez to Man City, Chelsea search for replacement
News.content:
Transfer deadline day has arrived with two of the biggest sagas of the summer still to be resolved: will Arsenal sign Julian Alvarez and could Enzo Fernandez be swapping Chelsea for Manchester City before tonight’s 11pm deadline?

Premier League champions Arsenal have pursued Alvarez all window but are running out of time to submit an offer to Atletico Madrid, despite selling Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to free up space for the 26-year-old forward. It means the Gunners could be left short in attack if they do not meet Atletico’s €150m asking price and so have explored alternatives, with Lyon’s Malick Fofana emerging as a late option.

Manchester City, meanwhile, will need to submit a bid that is higher than £120m to sign Fernandez from Chelsea and complete their midfield rebuild. Fernandez has been left out of Chelsea’s last two squads and Xabi Alonso’s side will not sell the Argentina international without a suitable replacement, with Monaco’s Lamine Camara, Roma’s Manu Kone and Bournemouth’s Alex Scott all on their radar.

Manchester United have still not signed a left back, while Liverpool’s business appears done after signing Bradley Barcola and rejecting Manchester City’s approach for Cody Gakpo. City have agreed a £60m deal with Everton to buy Iliman Ndiaye. That could have an impact on Everton’s pursuit of Richarlison, with Tottenham still wanting to sign a new forward too.

News.content:

Julia Roberts said she'd never forget Dolly Parton's response to her complaining on the set of the 1989 movie Steel Magnolias.

Parton, who died Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, appeared with Roberts, now 58, on The Oprah Winfrey Show in 1989 to promote the movie. In a clip from that appearance that has resurfaced in the wake of Parton’s death, Roberts shared that Parton had given her a crucial piece of advice during a sweltering day filming in the Louisiana summer heat.

“Everyone had ice on their wrist and was doing the whole thing, everyone was like, ‘It’s hot, can I get some water?’ And I finally just had to say, ‘Dolly, I mean, you’ve got a wig and the wool. Come on, it’s hot, sweat a little, you know? Just say ‘I’m hot,’ you know. ‘This is a drag!’” Roberts recalled to host Winfrey.

She continued: “And she said — I remember we were sitting on the porch, do you remember this? And she said to me, ‘When I was a little girl, I wanted to be famous and I wanted to be rich, and now I’m both those things. I’m not going to complain about it.’”

open image in gallery Julia Roberts has shared the piece of advice that Dolly Parton gave her at the beginning of her career, and she hasn’t forgotten it ( Sony )

open image in gallery Parton and Roberts appeared alongside Sally Field, Daryl Hannah, Shirley MacLaine and Olympia Dukakis in ‘Steel Magnolias’ ( Public domain )

Roberts said that she took the advice to never complain very seriously and that she’s “never forgotten it.”

“I thought, ‘Okay, I’m going to be quiet for the rest of the day,’” she said at the time.

“It was the way she said it, and I didn’t really do it her way, or else it’ll choke me up, but it was this thing and I’ve never forgotten it. And every time I go to complain or just kind of moan, I always hear Dolly sitting on the porch and saying that, and it kind of keeps you quiet.”

In the film, Parton played the Louisiana beauty salon owner Truvy Jones, while Roberts, who was only two years into her acting career at the time, played Shelby Eatenton-Latcherie, a young, headstrong bride.

The movie, which followed the lives of a group of women supporting each other through life’s ups and downs, also starred Sally Field, Daryl Hannah, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis, Tom Skerritt and Sam Shepard.

After the news of Parton’s death, Roberts paid tribute to in a statement, saying: “Dolly was a magical and joyous human. I hold knowing her as a treasure in my life. The sun has dimmed today.”

MacLaine, 92, wrote, “God sent her to us, and she has returned home.”

“Without exaggeration, Dolly Parton was one of the sharpest, funniest, and warmest people I’ve ever met,” Hannah wrote in her tribute.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton’s most memorable film performance was portraying the Louisiana beauty salon owner Truvy Jones in ‘Steel Magnolias’ ( Tri-Star Pictures )

open image in gallery The Queen of Country, Dolly Parton, died in Nashville following a ‘brief battle with cancer,’ her representative said ( PA )

“She is just the best example of how to be a great human. I’m sure we will all continue to discover more about her humble, important, and generous altruistic charity work which, she would barely ever mention.”

Field said: “If there are truly angels on earth, then we have just lost one. Dolly Parton. There will never be another.”

“I adored her with all my heart and will always cherish our time together. Forever. Rest in peace beautiful Dolly,” the tribute continued.

The movie was just one of Parton’s big-screen roles across her illustrious entertainment career. She also appeared in movies including 9 to 5, Rhinestone and The Beverly Hillbillies.

Parton's death was announced Tuesday by her nephew Bryan Seaver, who served as Parton’s head of security. Her representative later confirmed that she had died in Nashville, following a “brief battle” with cancer, surrounded by loved ones.

Singer Miley Cyrus, Parton’s goddaughter, remembered her “Aunt Dolly” as an “angel,” saying, “I will always love her and want to make her proud.

Former champion Stan Wawrinka lost to Italy's Matteo Berrettini 7-6(4) 7-6(3) 6-0 in the first round of the US Open , with the 41-year-old bidding an emotional farewell after his final grand slam before retiring at the end of the season.

In front of a packed crowd on Grandstand, Wawrinka repeatedly threatened to turn the ⁠match around before Berrettini, 30, found ways to shut the door, as the pair produced another rollercoaster after their dramatic clash at this year's Wimbledon.

The 2016 champion fell behind early but sparked the crowd into life, breaking to love when Berrettini served for the opening set to pull level. Wawrinka then earned a set point in a marathon ⁠game, but Berrettini survived four deuces to force a tiebreak. ​The ⁠younger player held his nerve again, winning three consecutive points to take the opener.

open image in gallery Stan Wawrinka said farewell to the US Open with a battling defeat ( AP )

The second set offered Wawrinka another opening as a brief rain interruption was followed by an `early break of Berrettini's serve. But Wawrinka could not make his advantage count. He had seven break points, ​including ⁠three set points, yet Berrettini repeatedly found ‌a way out before breaking back and forcing another tiebreak, which he won to move within a set of victory.

The third set brought no let-up, with the opening game stretching to 16 minutes after a frustrated Berrettini unsuccessfully challenged a call involving a possible double hit. Yet Berrettini, former world No 6, emerged from the long battle with the first of three breaks to serve up a bagel that ended Wawrinka's glittering grand slam career.

"It's been 20 years since the first time I came here. It was amazing for me to feel the New York vibes throughout the years. I found the way to play my best tennis here," Wawrinka said. Wawrinka's appearance in New York carried added significance after the three-time grand slam champion was initially left out of the singles field despite applying for a wildcard.

The decision prompted an outcry from fans, and he was eventually given a place after American Patrick Kypson withdrew with an injury. Wawrinka, who reached a career-high ranking of world No 3, had said before the tournament that ‌he was at peace with his career and simply grateful for one final opportunity at ​the grand slam he won 10 years ago.

"One of the reasons I played until 41 was to live these moments. I'm very grateful for this wildcard. It was very important for me to finish here, where I won a grand slam 10 years ago. I want to thank you all for all these years," an emotional Wawrinka added.

Berrettini, a ‌semi-finalist in New York in ​2019, will face Mariano Navone in the second ‌round after the Argentine produced the tournament's biggest ​upset by knocking out fourth seed Novak Djokovic in five sets on Sunday.

Meteorologists have decided Austen, Boelo and Chloe will be the first named storms of the 2026/27 season, after more than 40,000 public suggestions.

The UK’s Met Office, Ireland’s Met Éireann and the Dutch national weather forecasting service KNMI announced the full list of storm names on Tuesday.

The organisations have been naming storms since 2015, with the list running from early September to the following August, coinciding with the start of autumn when the likelihood of low-pressure systems and the potential for storms severe enough to be named increases.

Names featured include those in honour of a five-year-old weather enthusiast, a much-loved Labrador puppy, meteorological pioneers and Shaun the Sheep from the popular animation Wallace and Gromit. However, the Met Office said the purpose of naming storms is also serious, as it helps people prepare and stay safe in severe weather.

In the last year, four names were used from the list, reaching the letter D with Storm Dave on April 1.

The UK also saw impacts from a further three storms named by other European meteorological services – Storms Benjamin, Claudia and Goretti.

open image in gallery Shaun the Sheep from the popular animation Wallace and Gromit ( PA )

Under naming conventions used for storms in the North Atlantic, the list runs alphabetically, missing out Q, U, X, Y and Z.

The third name in this year’s list, Chloe, was selected by the Met Office after being put forward more than 120 times, including by the mother of a five-year-old weather enthusiast who is “fascinated by the weather” but can also “create a storm by herself” when she is tired.

The name Finn was suggested for a two-year-old boy described by his family as “wild and a force to be reckoned with”, while Ivy was nominated in honour of a nine-month-old Labrador puppy affectionately known as “the absolute destructor”.

Nicola was put forward as a tribute to a mother who has “weathered many a storm and only come out stronger”, while Theo was inspired by a cat who would hide before thunderstorms, leading his owner to joke that he could predict the weather.

Shaun also joined the list following a public vote that was run as part of a collaboration with the British animation studio Aardman, which was behind the beloved show Wallace and Gromit.

The aim of the collaboration was to reach new audiences and encourage conversations on preparedness for severe weather by combining the Met Office’s forecasting expertise with Aardman’s storytelling.

To mark its 90th anniversary, Met Éireann selected names that celebrate figures from its history, including Austen, in honour of Austen Nagle, the first director of the Irish Meteorological Service and Evelyn Murphy, the first woman to present the weather on Ireland’s national public service broadcaster RTE.

Meanwhile, KNMI picked names from more than 3,000 suggestions submitted by the public, including Boelo – a nearly extinct name from the east Groningen region that has been passed down through the nominator’s family for generations.

open image in gallery The storm names selected last year for the 2025/26 season ( Met Office )

Holly Clements, Met Office head of warnings and guidance, said: “For more than a decade, storm naming has helped us communicate the risks from severe weather more effectively.

“A named storm provides a clear focus for forecasts and warnings, helping more people understand the potential impacts and take action to protect themselves, their families and their property.”

Eoin Sherlock, Met Éireann head of forecasting division, said: “We know that naming storms makes it easier for people to track important and up-to-date forecast and safety-related information, as we can see from the levels of traffic and activity through our website and across social media platforms during storm events.

“2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the establishment of the Irish Meteorological Service and we are proud to be able to recognise some of the significant contributors to our history in the list of storm names this year.”

The Met Office said a number of factors were considered for including a name on the list, including how difficult it is to produce, if it has different meanings across the different countries, is connected to a public figure or could be controversial in any way.

Storms are given a name when they are deemed to have the potential to cause medium or high impacts in the UK, Ireland or the Netherlands, with wind the primary focus, although additional issues from rain or snow will also be looked at.

News.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis found guilty in Tupac murder case after decades of speculation
News.content:

A man has been found guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, marking the first conviction in a case that has gripped hip-hop fans for decades.

Duane “Keffe D” Davis, 63, was convicted on Monday of a single count of murder with a deadly weapon and could be sentenced to life in prison. The jury deliberated for less than 3 hours after a weekslong trial in Las Vegas.

For nearly three decades, the killing of Tupac Shakur was one of hip-hop's most enduring mysteries, a case marked by reluctant witnesses, dead suspects and questions about whether anyone would ever be held accountable.

After the verdict was read, Shakur's sister, Sekyiwa “Set” Shakur, cried and hugged the prosecutors. Also in the courtroom was Davis’ son, who covered his face with one hand.

Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors in closing arguments that Davis acquired a gun and “went hunting” for Shakur and Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight after they beat up Davis’ nephew earlier that night.

Palal acknowledged that Davis’ accounts of the killing evolved over the years but argued those differences reflected Davis’ changing motivations and efforts to protect himself. One critical detail, he said, remained consistent: Davis repeatedly placed himself inside a white Cadillac from which the shots were fired.

open image in gallery Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon ( AFP/Getty )

The panel of 16 jurors, four of whom are alternates, heard testimony from 24 prosecution witnesses and three defense witnesses over nine days.

“The core facts remain. The material facts remain,” Palal said.

The prosecution said Monday evening that the state would dismiss the gang enhancement part of the charge due to witness logistics.

The trial brought to a head a decades-old case that for years has drawn the attention of hip-hop fans and true crime experts alike. Shakur, who was considered one of the most influential rappers of all time, was in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996, and stopped at a red light when a white Cadillac pulled up beside him, and shots were fired. He died six days later from his wounds. Knight was also wounded but survived.

For years, nobody had been charged in the rapper’s death until Davis began making public statements, saying he was in the Cadillac and gave the gun to others in the backseat. Davis described the shooting as an act of retaliation after Knight and Shakur’s entourage beat up Davis’ nephew hours before the shooting.

Under Nevada law, someone who helps another person commit murder can be convicted of the crime. Davis is the only person still alive among the four men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac. The man who prosecutors say originally gave the gun to Davis is also dead.

Palal told jurors that if they believed Davis' statements, they did not have to be independently corroborated with additional evidence.

open image in gallery Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon ( Reuters )

Still, he pointed to the rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru, the fight with Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson and testimony that members of Shakur’s circle identified Anderson and Davis as suspects the night of the shooting. Witnesses had testified to the heated gang rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru, which were associated with dueling record companies Bad Boy Records and Death Row Records.

“Who fired is not the question,” Palal said. Prosecutors haven't argued that Davis pulled the trigger, but instead that he was criminally responsible because he provided the gun and ordered the attack.

Palal also argued the shooting was premeditated, pointing to testimony and Davis’ accounts that the group searched for Shakur before spotting him on the road and making a U-turn. “It’s a plan, not an impulse,” Palal said.

Palal held up Davis’ 2019 memoir, “Compton Street Legend,” and played an interview in which Davis encouraged people to buy it to get the “real truth.” Although the book contains a disclaimer saying some facts were changed, Palal argued that names, hotels and other details changed while the central account did not.

Palal also rejected the defense’s contention that Davis fabricated his accounts to make money. “It is an entirely different proposition to be profiting from a murder,” Palal said. “And that is what Mr. Davis is doing.”

Defense attorney Michael Sanft also turned to his client’s memoir during his closing argument. While reading an excerpt, he said the N-word aloud, prompting people watching in an overflow courtroom to recoil and shake their heads.

In multiple interviews, Davis said he handed the gun to the back seat, but in others as well as in his book, Davis wouldn’t say who pulled the trigger.

In a rebuttal argument, prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo pointed to a scrapbook Davis kept containing articles about Shakur.

“This guy's scrapbooking his murder, for God's sake,” DiGiacomo told jurors.

The prosecution's witnesses included a gang expert who described Davis as the shot caller that younger gang members had to obey. Sanft asked jurors if there was any evidence that Davis had ever called the shots before or after the shooting.

During the trial, investigators said a Las Vegas hotel bill was found at Davis’ residence during a police search, but it wasn’t clear when it was dated — or where that evidence is currently located.

The case is nearly 30 years old, which has affected the kind of evidence presented in court. Prosecutors warned jurors that material collected in the ’90s is different from what law enforcement collects today, including hotel surveillance video from the night of the shooting.

How Duane "Keffe D" Davis was caught

In the end, some of the most damaging evidence against the only man ever charged came from the man himself.

Duane "Keffe D" Davis spent years talking about the 1996 shooting with many people, including investigators, filmmakers and interviewers and through his memoir, "Compton Street Legend." Prosecutors used those accounts to build a murder case against him, while his attorney argued Davis had been telling stories for money and notoriety.

The prosecution's case centered on Davis' own words.

Over the years, Davis repeatedly placed himself inside the white Cadillac that pulled alongside Shakur and Death Row Records co-founder Marion "Suge" Knight on Sept. 7, 1996. In interviews with law enforcement and later public accounts, Davis described obtaining a gun and passing it to the backseat before shots were fired.

open image in gallery Duane Davis, center, and his attorney Michael Sanft are led back to a courtroom to hear his sentencing date after a jury found Davis guilty of first-degree murder in his trial related to the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, at Clark County District Court Regional Justice Center, Monday, Aug. 31, 2026, in Las Vegas. Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Pool via REUTERS ( Reuters )

Prosecutors did not accuse Davis of pulling the trigger. Instead, they argued he organized the group, provided the gun and helped carry out a retaliatory attack after Shakur and Knight's entourage beat Davis' nephew, Orlando "Baby Lane" Anderson, at the MGM Grand earlier that night.

Under Nevada law, someone who aids or helps another person commit murder can also be held criminally responsible.

What did Davis say about the shooting?

Davis began providing some of his most consequential details during a 2008 interview with law enforcement while authorities were investigating the 1997 killing of Shakur's rap rival, The Notorious B.I.G.

Davis said he was riding in the front passenger seat of the Cadillac with three other men, including his nephew. He described spotting Shakur and Knight, making a U-turn and pulling alongside their BMW.

"If we would have been on my side, I would have blasted," Davis told investigators. Instead, Davis said, he passed the gun to the backseat.

open image in gallery Michael Sanft, attorney for Duane Davis, makes closing arguments in the Duane Davis murder trial, related to the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, in Clark County District Court at the Regional Justice Center in Las Vegas, Nevada, U.S., August 31, 2026. REUTERS/Steve Marcus/Pool ( Reuters )

He later spoke publicly about the killing and described it in his 2019 memoir. Prosecutors played jurors an interview in which Davis promoted the book as a way to get the "real truth."

Davis' accounts varied on some details, including who ultimately fired the shots. But prosecutors emphasized that he repeatedly put himself inside the Cadillac and described his role in supplying the weapon.

Those public statements proved critical.

Why did it take nearly 30 years to bring charges?

Police had long suspected that Shakur's killing was retaliation for the MGM Grand beating, but investigators struggled to build a case they could prosecute.

Witnesses were reluctant to cooperate. Knight, who was sitting beside Shakur when the shots were fired, did not provide investigators with an account that led to charges. Other people believed to have been inside the Cadillac died over the ensuing years.

Davis spoke to investigators off the record in 2008 under an agreement with federal authorities and again with Las Vegas police in 2009. The unusual circumstances surrounding those interviews complicated whether his statements could be used against him.

But Davis later began discussing the killing publicly, including in documentaries, interviews and his memoir. Prosecutors argued those public disclosures allowed them to use statements he had made years earlier.

A renewed Las Vegas police investigation eventually led to Davis' arrest in 2023.

What did Davis' defense argue?

Defense attorney Michael Sanft asked jurors to reject the very statements prosecutors considered their strongest evidence.

Sanft argued that Davis had exaggerated or fabricated accounts of his involvement for money and notoriety. He characterized his client's statements as braggadocio and fiction rather than confessions.

More importantly, Sanft argued investigators had failed to independently prove that Davis was even in Las Vegas on the night Shakur was shot.

He pointed to the absence of surveillance footage, phone records and other physical or documentary evidence placing Davis inside the Cadillac.

"They have nothing in this case that says that man was here in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996," Sanft told jurors, pointing toward Davis during his closing argument.

Sanft also attacked the integrity of the decades-old investigation, arguing that missing records, questionable police practices and the involvement of multiple law enforcement agencies made the prosecution's case unreliable.

Prosecutors countered that Davis' admissions did not have to be independently corroborated if jurors believed them. They also pointed to circumstantial evidence they said supported his account, including the MGM Grand beating, the gang rivalry surrounding the two groups and testimony about the events leading up to the shooting.

What happens to Davis now?

Moments after the verdict, Judge Carli Kierny ordered Davis to be held without bail while he awaits sentencing on Oct. 13. Davis raised his hand and said, "Excuse me," before asking for the return of jewelry, a phone and other belongings.

"And I would like to appeal this matter," Davis told the judge.

Kierny told him an appeal would come after sentencing.

Prosecutors also voluntarily dismissed an extra prison sentence related to gang activity after the verdict, citing logistical issues involving a witness. That eliminated the need for jurors to consider an additional phase of the case.
