Deadline day has arrived for the Premier League with clubs remaining eager to add players and move them on with the pressure of early results tipping the balance.

The Premier League has spent over £2.5bn this summer, with Morgan Rogers at £117m the biggest signing of the summer.

Other big signings that topped the £100m mark include Elliot Anderson (£116m) to Manchester City and Sandro Tonali (£100m) to Tottenham, while Liverpool captured Bradley Barcola on Monday for a fee that could rise to £123m.

But more big-money deals could yet go through before the window closes – Manchester City continue to chase Enzo Fernandez of Chelsea, though appear to have missed out on Cody Gakpo.

Here’s everything we know as the window prepares to slam shut.

When is the Premier League summer 2026 transfer window?

The transfer window opened for business on Monday 15 June and the deadline is on Tuesday 1 September in England, the window shuts at 11pm BST.

There is also a two-hour grace period after the window shuts, which will allow paperwork to be submitted.

When is the 2026 summer transfer window in Scotland?

Like the English transfer window, the window officially opened on 15 June, but the window north of the border shuts on 3 September at 5pm BST, two days after the Premier League deadline.

When is the 2026 WSL summer transfer window?

The Women's Super League transfer window opened on Tuesday 16 June and will close on Thursday 3 September, with a later deadline of 11pm BST.

When does the transfer window close in Europe?

The transfer window for LaLiga shuts at 10.59pm on 1 September, while Bundesliga clubs must buy and sell players before a 31 August deadline at 7pm.

Serie A clubs have until 1 September, with an 8pm deadline.

When is the winter transfer window?

Mid-season additions will be available when the transfer window re-opens in England on 1 January, 2027 and ti closes on 1 February once again at the later time of 11pm GMT.

In Scotland, the window will open four days after the Premier League on 5 January and then shuts on 4 February at 5pm GMT.

In the WSL, the window opens on 4 January and will close on 4 February, the same day as in Scotland.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” said Arsenal head coach Arteta. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it (my energy) now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Despite ugly ending to his Argentina career, Messi redefined beautiful game
News.content:
To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely-scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pele’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

Sports.title: The 10 biggest transfers that could still go through on deadline day, including Alvarez to Arsenal and Enzo to Man City
Sports.content:
LET the scramble for last-minute new signings begin!

The Premier League’s top sides could all be active on transfer deadline day today, with the futures of several players still undecided.



Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea, and big-spenders Tottenham are reportedly still in the market to add to their squads.

SunSport looks at the 10 biggest transfers that could STILL happen, starting with the summer’s biggest saga of all.



Julian Alvarez to Arsenal

Will he join or won’t he?

That’s been the question on Arsenal fans’ lips all summer, with the Argentinian being the Premier League champions’ top target in this window.

Of course, he wants Barcelona, but the forward’s club Atletico Madrid don’t want to sell him to their LaLiga rivals.

Reports say that the Gunners are waiting on Alvarez to change his mind and give them the thumbs up and are ready to seal a record British transfer.

However, the fact he is back training with Atletico, following a fan fallout, suggests he might stay put.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Enzo Fernandez to Man City

In what could be a British record £140m transfer fee, Man City are still pursuing Chelsea’s out-of-favour Argentinian Enzo Fernandez.

The midfielder was left out of Xabi Alonso’s squad against Brighton – with the Spaniard tight-lipped about the World Cup winner’s future.

City have finally opened talks with the Blues over reuniting Enzos Fernandez and Maresca.

With Chelsea set to play hard ball, however, this could go right to the wire.

Iliman Ndiaye to Man City

Maresca’s side dramatically hijacked Tottenham’s swoop for Everton star Iliman Ndiaye on Monday.



It is believed Everton had struck an agreement in principle with Spurs for Ndiaye to join for £60million.

But after seemingly missing out on Cody Gakpo, City pivoted to Ndiaye, leaving Spurs’ hopes in tatters.

With Roberto De Zerbi’s side having moved on to Mykhaylo Mudryk, Ndiaye to City feels likely.



Manu Kone, Lamine Camara & Alex Scott to Chelsea

Now, Chelsea are preparing themselves for the departure of Fernandez.

They have contacted several targets to bolster their midfield, including France star Manu Kone.

Transfer expert Fabrizio Romano reports that Chelsea have contacted Kone’s camp to sound out a move from Roma, although there’s been no official bid yet.

Talks with Monaco ace Lamine Camara have reportedly stalled, according to Onze Mondial.

A deal was discussed, but Chelsea have since cooled their interest. But, that could all change.



Alex Scott of Bournemouth looks like a no-goer, though.

The Cherries’ sporting director Thiago Pinto said the playmaker won’t be sold, even though he will enter the final year of his contract in 2027.

Who knows? A monster bid might change that.



Cody Gakpo to Man City or Spurs

Gakpo had looked likely to leave Liverpool all summer, with both Man City and Tottenham heavily linked.

The Dutch winger even agreed personal terms with the former, but Liverpool are reluctant to sanction an £85million deal until they’ve found a replacement.

They completed their huge £123m deal for PSG superstar Bradley Barcola on Monday – but that deal is viewed as separate to Gakpo’s situation.

And, finding someone to fill his shoes in such a short time does look tricky.

Spurs thought they had Gakpo in the bag, until City hijacked their move. Maybe they’ll still have hope, if City switch their attentions to someone else and Liverpool feel the offer is too good to refuse.



Ismaila Sarr or Yankuba Minteh to Liverpool

Which leads us to Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr.

Liverpool see the Senegalese star as the perfect Gakpo replacement, and have reportedly bid around £50million for his services.



That’s not enough for the Eagles, though, who are holding out for £75million, say reports.

The Reds have also had bids for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh rejected too.

The Seagulls want over £60million for the Gambian.



Lewis Hall to Man Utd

Have the Red Devils left a move for Lewis Hall too late?

We won’t know until midnight. But Michael Carrick is said to wanted to sign the player all summer.

Newcastle have insisted the left-back is not for sale, even if United offer an astronomical amount on transfer deadline day.

With Luke Shaw now 31, cover is desperately needed. Will that force United’s hand to send the Toon a huge offer?

Folarin Balogun to Everton

It had appeared that Richarlison was set for a homecoming to the Toffees.



But following an explosive Instagram post on Monday night, it appears that the Brazilian will be remaining at Spurs after all.

Now, in a twist to that saga, Everton are said to have sent a £40m bid to Monaco for former Arsenal striker Folarin Balogun.

With a deal for Richarlison seemingly haven fallen through, Balogun is set to be David Moyes’ new man up top.



Jack Grealish to Everton

Finally, the future of Jack Grealish, the Premier League’s former poster boy, who really needs the Everton move to come through to kick-start his career.

The latest from The Athletic is that Grealish is set for a medical at Everton after the Toffees met City’s demands.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

This would offset the departure of Ndiaye, with Grealish slotting in on the left-side.

Sunderland are also attentive to a potential deal, and could offer the former Aston Villa star a permanent contract – but Everton appear to have won the race.

Sports.title: Arsenal considering deadline day transfer for Lyon’s Malick Fofana with Gunners seeking Martinelli replacement
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are considering a move to sign Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The Gunners are looking to add attacking reinforcements before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.



Fofana, 21, is on the club’s list of potential additions and transfer chiefs are mulling over making a late move for the Belgian.

Arsenal have already lost Leandro Trossard to Besiktas this summer and are set to sell Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal in a £60m deal too.



The Emirates outfit spent much of their summer pursuing Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior to upgrade their left flank.

But that move was scuppered when the Brazilian penned a new six-year deal to tie him down to the Bernabeu.

Arsenal also explored signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, but the England international ultimately joined Chelsea for £117m.

Fofana represents a market opportunity for Mikel Arteta and Co, who need to add more depth to their left flank.

New signing Christos Tzolis has impressed since his £34m arrival from Club Brugge earlier in the window, but the Greek has little back-up in his position.

Fofana, whose current contract runs until 2028, scored just two goals in 16 games across all competitions for Lyon last season, but has started the new campaign in eye-catching form.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The former Gent ace has already matched his goal tally from last term in only six appearances across Ligue 1 and Champions League qualifying.

Arsenal have also been working on a deal to sign Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid.

However, their chase has hit a stumbling block with the Argentine set on joining Barcelona over the Gunners.

Atletico, however, have no intention of selling their star striker to their fierce Spanish rivals.

Sports.title: ‘I don’t know Jamie Carragher’ – Sunderland ace Wilson Isidor’s blunt response to Sky Sports pundit after relegation tip
Sports.content:
WILSON ISIDOR does not care about Jamie Carragher’s grim Sunderland prediction and claims he has no clue who the Liverpool legend is.

The striker instead vowed to ram the words of any doubters down their throats by proving last season was no “miracle”.



Carragher called Sunderland “arrogant” after the opening day defeat at Ipswich before tipping them for relegation due to the extra demands of the Europa League.

The Black Cats responded with a 1-0 victory over Fulham at the Stadium of Light on Sunday thanks to supersub Isidor’s strike.



Asked to respond to the Sky Sports pundit’s remarks, the spiky Haiti star said: “I don’t know Jamie Carragher. If I don’t know, I don’t have to listen to him.

“People can think about that, but the most important thing that the club showed is they kept the same players who were there last year, and that’s a big, big point from the club that people don’t realise.

“We want to show everybody that last season was not a miracle and Sunderland are really strong and proud to be in the Premier League and also deserve to be in it.

“We want to keep our level like that and to show that the place of Sunderland is in the Premier League and in the upper part of the ranking.”

Isidor only scored six goals during last season’s magical seventh place finish having played second fiddle to Brian Brobbey for the majority of it.

The 26-year-old has been restricted to two cameos off the bench so far this term – but he pleaded with boss Regis Le Bris to unleash him alongside the Dutch powerhouse when they head to Brentford next.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He added: “That’s the… not the dream, but a lot of people want that, and me the first.

“Brian is a different player than me, totally opposite, and the combination of us two can be really amazing.

“That’s the manager’s decision. As I say, he takes his decision, but I would be really happy to play with Brian.

“I just want to score goals. I don’t set a target. I’ve got a good relationship with Brian, so that’s not a bad thing. We know that we have to fight for one spot, but now the gaffer makes the decision.



“Whether it’s me or him, the most important thing for me is to be focused on my performance, on what I can bring on the team, and of course that the team wins.”

One man unlikely to be part of Sunderland’s push this term is winger Jocelin Ta Bi as he closes in on a move to Championship side Burnley.

The 21-year-old, who arrived on Wearside from Israeli side Maccabi Netanya in January, was not included in the squad against Fulham and looks set to switch to Turf Moor on loan.

Sports.title: PSG star earning £150k-a-week turns up to training in £7,000 Peugeot van as fans left stunned
Sports.content:
EVEN a back-to-back Champions League winning midfielder is not above driving around a car worth £7,000.

Yes, Joao Neves has been spotted leaving PSG training in a Peugeot van.



Unless he is a painter and decorator on the side, we can only speculate as to why!

But it wasn’t a brand new van either. It was 2021 Peugeot Partner, available for around £7,000.



Given that Neves is on around £150,000-a-week in the French capital, he probably picked it up with the spare change he had in his pocket!

Most footballers love to flash their expensive cars around the training ground, but clearly Neves is cut from a different cloth.



The TikTok shows the humble star stopping to sign autographs for fans before bolting off in his little van.

Still only 21-years-old, he has been a revelation under Luis Enrique in Paris since his £60million move from Benfica two years ago.

Neves has formed one-half of one of the most formidable midfield partnerships in Europe alongside compatriot Vitinha.

But there has been plenty of change at the club this summer, mostly in the forward line.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ibrahima Mbaye has left for around £45m to Aston Villa while Bradley Barcola‘s move to Liverpool could end up being worth £123m.

However, both Maghnes Akliouche and Ferran Torres have joined the club in their places.

Sports.title: Robert Sanchez to LEAVE Chelsea just days after Blues signed Emi Martinez as Cesc Fabregas’ Como poach goalkeeper
Sports.content:
ROBERT SANCHEZ is set to leave Chelsea and join Como on loan, according to reports.

The Spaniard was replaced as Blues No1 after Xabi Alonso‘s side signed Emi Martinez from Aston Villa.



And, having immediately lost his spot to the Argentine in the 4-3 win over Brighton on Sunday, Sanchez is now leaving Stamford Bridge.

According to transfer guru Fabrizio Romano, Como have agreed a loan deal with Chelsea to take Sanchez for the season.



The three-cap Spain goalkeeper is likely to replace French stopper Jean Butez as first-choice at Como.

Backup keeper Noel Tornqvist, meanwhile, is set to leave Cesc Fabregas‘ side for Monza.

This is not the first time that Chelsea have done business with Como this summer.

Trevoh Chalobah left the Blues for Fabregas’ side in a £26million deal last month.

With Sanchez gone, Martinez is the undisputed No1 at Chelsea for this season.

The Argentine will be backed up by Mike Penders, who played in the League Cup against Luton last Thursday.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Chelsea could still let several more players leave ahead of the transfer deadline.

Manchester City have finally opened contact regarding a blockbuster move for Enzo Fernandez.

And Tottenham are nearing a double swoop for Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk.

Adarabioyo is on the brink of a permanent switch to the North Londoners.

Mudryk, meanwhile, is set to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk boss Roberto De Zerbi on loan.

Sports.title: How Liverpool can line up if Ismaila Sarr completes transfer in dream deadline day scenario
Sports.content:
Liverpool's new era under Andoni Iraola has begun with more questions than answers, and with transfer deadline day upon them. The club now face a critical opportunity to shape the rest of their season.

Two draws from two Premier League matches, a 2-2 stalemate against Newcastle on the opening weekend and another frustrating share of the spoils against Nottingham Forest at Anfield on Saturday, have left supporters searching for reasons for optimism.

There are a few. Teenage duo Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz have caught the eye, offering Iraola a pair of assured youngsters ready to stake a genuine claim in the first XI. Meanwhile, Bradley Barcola's long-awaited arrival from PSG finally adds a cutting edge on the left flank that the squad has been crying out for.

What happens before the window slams shut, however, could prove decisive. The right signings now could give Iraola the tools he needs to push Liverpool up the table, and potentially transform what has been a stuttering campaign into something far more promising.

‌



Here, we examine what Liverpool's starting XI could look like if they achieve their objectives on transfer deadline day.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool news: Ismaila Sarr transfer update as winger gives green light to move READ MORE :

Goalkeeper

Alisson Becker arrived at the Reds in August 2018 and has established himself as, arguably, the finest goalkeeper in the club's history. While he has contended with his fair share of fitness setbacks in recent campaigns, on his day, there are few superior to the Brazilian, even at 33.

Giorgi Mamardashvili has stepped in with mixed results, but the Georgian has ultimately fallen short of expectations thus far. The club are nearing a £30m agreement for 18-year-old goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans, though he is anticipated to stay in Belgium for the upcoming campaign.

‌



This means Alisson will remain between the posts for the rest of this season, as he has done for the club's opening two fixtures.

Defence

French centre-back Jeremy Jacquet, snapped up from Rennes in January for £60m, looks set to be Virgil van Dijk's new partner at the heart of defence after being named in the starting XI for the opening two matches of the campaign.

At full-back, with Conor Bradley still sidelined following an injury sustained against Arsenal towards the end of last season, Jeremie Frimpong is expected to retain his place at right-back.

View 4 Images Jeremy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk before Liverpool vs Como in pre-season (Image: Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



That said, the Dutch international's displays will need to improve following an underwhelming start to the season. Some supporters have suggested Dominik Szoboszlai could return to right-back after filling in there last campaign.

However, Iraola has so far preferred Liverpool's No. 8 operating in central areas. On the opposite flank, Milos Kerkez will be the clear first-choice left-back in the wake of Andy Robertson's exit to Spurs.

Midfield

The central pairing for Iraola arguably selects itself, with Ryan Gravenberch lining up alongside Szoboszlai, while the Dutchman occupies a deeper No. 6 role. Though the former was left out of Saturday's stalemate with Forest after gifting two goals in the defeat to the Magpies seven days prior.

‌



Operating ahead of that duo will be Florian Wirtz, with the German playmaker afforded freedom to drift and combine with the front three, as he demonstrated to reasonable effect in the 2-2 draw with Forest.

Liverpool have other options in the centre of the pitch, including Alexis Mac Allister, who can compete with Gravenberch for the central midfield berth. Yet they are not exactly overflowing with first-team players vying for that role.

View 4 Images Liverpool attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz. (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

Despite Curtis Jones's exit to Inter Milan, the club are not believed to be looking to further strengthen their engine room during this window.

‌



Stefan Bajcetic is also thought to be on the verge of departing on a permanent basis, while Harvey Elliott is reportedly heading out of Anfield on loan to Valencia. That leaves an injured Wataru Endo, alongside James McConnell and Trey Nyoni, to bolster Iraola's central unit.

Attack

The formidable pairing of Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak is yet to get off the ground due to injuries, and that partnership will have to wait until the former makes a full recovery from a ruptured Achilles before it can truly flourish.

As a result, Isak, who netted his first goal of the campaign at the weekend against Forest, will be supported by new recruit Bradley Barcola on the left, with Cody Gakpo's impending switch to Manchester City appearing to be only a matter of time.

View 4 Images Liverpool have been linked with Crystal Palace attacker Ismaila Sarr (Image: Photo by Sebastian Frej/Getty Images)

‌



Barcola's deputy will be teenage sensation Rio Ngumoha. On the right, it seems to be a straight choice between Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr and Brighton's Yankuba Minteh.

The Reds are yet to find a replacement for Mohamed Salah on that flank, with Minteh attracting considerable interest. For now, Sarr appears the most likely candidate, with Liverpool already testing Palace's resolve with a £50m bid.

His arrival would offer Liverpool considerable Premier League experience in attack and see the Reds finally replace club icon Salah.

Liverpool's potenital starting XI: Alisson, Frimpong, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Barcola, Sarr, Isak.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta cites Aston Villa moment as the inspiration behind Arsenal's win
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta cites Aston Villa moment as the inspiration behind Arsenal's win

Arsenal avoid a repeat of last season' heartbreaking loss at Aston Villa with Mikel Arteta admitting the hurt had motivated Monday night's performance

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal made it two wins from two at Villa Park

Mikel Arteta hailed a “massive win” and then revealed Arsenal were fired up by last year’s heartbreak. The Gunners lost at Villa Park last season when Emiliano Buendia got a last-gasp winner to leave Arsenal shell-shocked.

‌



But the reigning champions made it two straight wins and a perfect start to the defence of their title thanks to Bukayo Saka’s second half goal.

‌



Arsenal boss Arteta said: “Really happy, it's a massive win. It's a tough place to come and earn three points. I think we deserved it. We had a great performance. I know how tough it is to win here. Every big team has struggled against them because they are so good.

‌



"I always trust my players. The level depends on the moment as well. Last year, we lost here in a really difficult way. That was still in the tummy. Last year was the same, we know how difficult it is to earn points in this league."

Arteta brought on Ezri Konsa against his old club to a mixed reception while Eberechi Eze came on at half time to change the game.

‌



"Ebs creates the action that wins us the game. Ezri, as well, really composed and really calm with every decision he made. I'm really happy with all of them,” said Arteta.

Arteta admitted that Arsenal could still move in the market on deadline day after effectively turning his phone off before Villa. He added: “I disconnected for a day. My focus had to be on the game, we have the right people at the club to look after that."

Saka said: “Very very tough game. It's not easy coming here, we knew that, and they made it hard for us so it feels great to come out with the win.

‌



View 2 Images Emi Buendia scored a dramatic late winner in this fixture last season (Image: PA)

“One goal is normally enough for us because we're so solid at the back. Once we got the first, we could have got the second. We had two penalty shouts that didn't go our way.”

Villa lost without a shot on target and did not manage one in their opener at Brighton either after a big summer of change.

Article continues below

Boss Unai Emery said: “To lose one match is painful, but we must try to get positive things. There are 38 matches, we have played two and have no points, but hopefully we can get better. We can feel confidence because the way we want to build a team is by competing like today.”

Sports.title: Liverpool complete transfer and reject £30m bid as Reds get busy before deadline
Sports.content:
Liverpool complete transfer and reject £30m bid as Reds get busy before deadline

Liverpool have sanctioned an exit and stood firm on the interest of their young midfielder following a bid from Nottingham Forest

View 2 Images Trey Nyoni was the subject of a transfer bid from Nottingham Forest (Image: Matt West/Shutterstock)

Liverpool have confirmed the permanent departure of Stefan Bajcetic to former club Celta Vigo - and have rejected a bid from Nottingham Forest for young midfielder Trey Nyoni. The 19‑year‑old was one of the standout performers during pre‑season.

‌



Having made his senior debut in the FA Cup in February 2024 and his Premier League debut against Tottenham Hotspur last December, Nyoni now has 21 appearances for the Reds. He was handed his first minutes of the new campaign in the 2-2 draw with Forest at Anfield last weekend.

‌



After being an unused substitute in the opener against Newcastle United, Nyoni replaced Alexis Mac Allister in the 77th minute - and appears to have left a lasting impression on Forest. So much so that they launched a £30million bid for the midfielder, according to The Times.

‌



The bid of £25m plus £5m in add-ons was swiftly rejected by Liverpool. Oliver Glasner's side are looking to sign a replacement for Elliot Anderson, who joined Manchester City for £116m.

However, Nyoni is viewed as a valued member of the squad despite his limited involvement so far, and he is expected to play a more significant role this season following Curtis Jones' exit.

Cody Gakpo to STAY at Liverpool as Man City make Enzo Fernandez top priority READ MORE :

Liverpool complete blockbuster Bradley Barcola transfer in huge coup for Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Meanwhile, Bajcetic has returned to Celta for an undisclosed fee. Liverpool acquired his services from the Spanish side back in 2021. Bajcetic's time at Anfield was disrupted by a calf injury that derailed his development and ruled him out for most of the 2023–24 season.

The 21‑year‑old then struggled to make an impact during loan spells at Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas.

A club statement confirming his exit, read: "Stefan Bajcetic has completed a permanent transfer from Liverpool to Celta Vigo. The midfielder returns to the Spanish club after five-and-a-half years with the Reds in which he made 22 senior appearances and scored once.

‌



"Bajcetic arrived on Merseyside from Celta in February 2021 and quickly progressed through the ranks at the club’s Academy. He debuted for Liverpool under Jurgen Klopp as a second-half substitute during the 9-0 Anfield win over AFC Bournemouth in August 2022, aged 17.

View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic has left Liverpool (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"A first goal followed for Bajcetic in a 3-1 Premier League victory away at Aston Villa on Boxing Day that same year, and overall he featured 19 times that season. However, injury issues limited him to only three appearances in the next campaign.

‌



"Bajcetic played 33 games across loan spells with Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas during 2024-25, though was again unable to take to the pitch during 2025-26. A deal has now been agreed for the 21-year-old to return to Celta in a permanent move. Everyone at LFC wishes Stefan the best of luck for the future."

In addition to Bajcetic, Ibrahima Konate, Andy Robertson, Mohamed Salah and Rhys Williams have all departed this summer. In terms of incomings, Iraola has been backed with Victor Munoz, Ronald Araujo, Jeremy Jacquet and Bradley Barcola.

Sports.title: Arsenal battle to Aston Villa win but question remains ahead of transfer deadline day
Sports.content:
Arsenal battle to Aston Villa win but question remains ahead of transfer deadline day

Arsenal battled to three points over Aston Villa courtesy of Bukayo Saka's second-half strike but questions persist over their need for more firepower

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka's strike was enough to earn Arsenal the win

It was not pretty but it still felt like a big win for Arsenal. Bukayo Saka got the second half winner as the champions were really made to work hard for their win at Villa Park.

‌



But this is never an easy place and it did raise question marks for Arsenal as to whether they still need a bit of extra quality and X Factor before the transfer window shuts on Tuesday.

‌



Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has spent £164m this summer on Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa - who came on to a mixed reception against his old club - but they still do not seem to have solved the most glaring issue of all. They lack a top quality left winger, a bit of spark and magic to match the endeavour and battling qualities which they showed in abundance against Aston Villa.

‌



Villa is a work in progress on and off the pitch. The North Stand is closed for redevelopment while they increase the capacity inside Villa Park to 50,000 for Euro 2028.

Emery’s annual summer rebuild on the pitch has seen major departures - including Ezri Konsa who joined Arsenal plus the likes of Youri Tielemans, Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne - while new arrivals Nicolas Jackson and Zion Suzuki were given their debuts.

‌



Villa looked a shambles when they were thrashed 4-0 at Brighton on the opening weekend but Emery is used to working miracles and the stadium was pumped for the first home game of the season. It was Villa who went close early on. Emiliano Buendia crashed a shot against the crossbar from 20 yards while Arsenal’s players were busy appealing for a foul which was not given.

Last year, it was Buendia who scored the injury time winner for Villa against Arsenal in this fixture which left the visiting players crushed. The Argentina forward was clearly in the mood again.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has been eyeing a striker all summer

‌



Arsenal went back to their tried and trusted formula of set-pieces. Riccardo Calafiori saw a near post header brilliantly saved by Villa keeper Suzuki but referee Jarred Gillett had already blown for a foul with Gabriel all over John McGinn at the back post.

The new purge on penalty box grappling is certainly not going to help Arsenal. Arsenal were certainly not producing the free-flowing football of their first game of the season against Coventry.

Christos Tzolis was booked for a pull-back on Matty Cash. The Arsenal winger then had an escape after he did the same to McGinn to stop a break but referee Gillett played an advantage and let it go.

‌



You can understand why Arsenal fans are concerned that selling Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli might leave them short on the left wing. They were certainly lacking a spark but that was all over the pitch.

View 3 Images Unai Emery's side remain without a win, without a goal and without a shot on target this season

It was no surprise when Tzolis was subbed at half time for Eberechi Eze. The great irony was that last season Eze was hooked at half time at Villa Park after a poor 45 minutes. Now, Eze was answering the SOS. It is obvious Arsenal have not solved the left-sided problem.

‌



Arsenal thought they had a breakthrough when Ian Maatsen bundled into Bukayo Saka and referee Gillett gave a penalty. But VAS ruled it was outside the box and a free kick was given instead. Martin Odegaard’s effort hit the side netting.

But the visitors eventually got their breakthrough after 59 minutes. Cristian Mosquera got the move going, Eze played in Calafiori and his clever pull back found Saka in the box and he forced home from close range.

Eze made a huge difference and that was also Saka’s second goal of the season. It was certainly not pretty but they really had to dig deep.

Sports.content:
Arsenal launch last-minute £50m transfer push as Mikel Arteta races against deadline

Arsenal have Belgium winger Malick Fofana on their shortlist with the player having been offered to the Gunners by Lyon

View 2 Images Malick Fofana could join Arsenal before the transfer deadline (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are pushing for a late signing, with Lyon winger Malick Fofana on their shortlist. The 21-year-old was put forward to the club ahead of Tuesday's transfer deadline.

‌



The Gunners are intent on adding another attacker to provide cover for Christos Tzolis, aiming to avoid Eberechi Eze becoming the obvious fallback option should they miss out on Fofana. Arsenal have already finalised exits for Gabriel Martinelli - set to join Al Hilal in a deal worth around £60million, Gabriel Jesus, who will move to Barcelona for £8.6m plus £4.3m in add‑ons, and Fabio Vieira, who is heading to Hamburger SV in a £7.7m transfer.

‌



Leandro Trossard has also left the Emirates, leaving Mikel Arteta short of options on the left flank. Attempts to secure a deal for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez have so far been unsuccessful.

‌



What is happening to Villa Park? Aston Villa redevelopment work explained as Arsenal visit READ MORE :

A wide‑player addition such as Fofana would represent the fourth piece of business Andrea Berta is working to complete before Tuesday's 11pm deadline. Mirror Football understands Lyon are demanding a fee in the region of £50m with Arsenal still in talks with the 21‑year‑old's representatives.

However, should a deal fail to come to fruition before the transfer deadline, failing to land a left winger to support Tzolis and fill the void left by departing duo Martinelli and Jesus will undoubtedly be considered a significant shortcoming. Berta is already under the microscope for the club's inability, thus far, to pinpoint and secure a genuine upgrade in the wide-left position.

Bradley Barcola attracted admiration from Arsenal, but a price tag in excess of £120m was never going to be entertained. Jeremy Monga was another highly-regarded target whom they made approaches for, yet the club were unwilling to meet the asking price - something Manchester City had no hesitation in doing.

‌



Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has reaffirmed that Arsenal remain steadfast in their commitment to a self-sustaining model, while insisting this does not mean agreeing to sales that are not in the club's best interests.

View 2 Images Arsenal have so far been unable to agree a deal for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"That's what we are trying to get as a club but the balance has to be right," Arteta said. "There are areas that we have to improve to hit those numbers. And if it's not with sales, because maybe we don't want.

"We have to sell what we want to sell as well, not just to sell. And then when we want to sell as well, we have to be very careful because some of the assets, after maybe they grow and we still want them.

"So maybe we can grow in other areas across the club as well. And commercially, we've done incredible. The fan base that we have is incredible.

Article continues below

"Our mass revenue is incredible. And there are other ways to grow and that's the club's strategy. But we want to improve in all of them, obviously, because it's going to give us a bigger room to be stronger financially."

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes in talks over new Man Utd contract to make him club's best-paid star
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes in talks over new Man Utd contract to make him club's best-paid star

Manchester United are set to make Bruno Fernandes their top earner when he signs his next deal as the Portugal star continues to prove his worth at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes' value is set to be rewarded with a huge pay bump

Manchester United are ready to make Bruno Fernandes their highest earner after the playmaker underlined his talismanic status with a hat-trick on Sunday.

‌



Fernandes, just days on from being named the PFA Player of the Year, scored three times in United's 5-2 rout of Ipswich at Old Trafford. The Portugal star was on hand to net their equaliser before the side ran riot in the second half.

‌



Fernandes signed new terms with United in 2022 and 2024, the expiry date of his contract was only extended by a year on each occasion, but his salary increased significantly. The Sun report that his next deal could see him earn around £350,000-a-week

‌



The ex-Sporting Lisbon man currently earns £300,000-a-week. Marcus Rashford is United’s highest earner on a weekly wage of £325,000, but he's spent the last 18 months away from Manchester before returning to the fold.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

United have attempted to change their wage structure, adopting more of a measured approach, but those at the club accept that Fernandes is performing to an incredibly high level and is deserving of a major pay bump.

‌



As well as the PFA award, Fernandes also claimed the Football Writers’ Association Player of the Year gong midway through last season, where he broke the record for assists in a single Premier League campaign. He also won an unprecedented fifth Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year award in May.

Fernandes was linked with the exit door previously as a move to Saudi Arabia was discussed for around £80million, but Ruben Amorim blocked any exit.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford remains Man Utd's highest earner

‌



That has proved a shrewd move with Fernandes continuing to prove inspirational for United and was key in their return to form under Michael Carrick last season.

Gary Neville waxed lyrical about Fernandes following Sunday's exploits, hailing him as the best piece of recruitment since 2013. “He is the best signing post Sir Alex Ferguson by an absolute mile," he said on his podcast. "He has got the guts, the courage, the belief to play for Manchester United, the numbers he has delivered with assists and goals. He's an outstanding player, he really is.”

Fernandes has scored 110 goals in 329 appearances for United since he signed from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020.

Sports.title: Why is Antonelli taking grid penalties on home soil in Italy?
Sports.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to be in contention for victory on home soil at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

Antonelli will start at the back of the grid as he will exceed the limit of four power units that can be used in a season before incurring grid penalties.

It means the Mercedes driver could see his 59-point lead over team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton cut significantly, while a third consecutive win for McLaren's Lando Norris could enable the reigning world champion to make major inroads into his 83-point deficit to Antonelli.

With Mercedes having confirmed that Antonelli is taking a grid penalty for changing his engine at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 explain why the world championship leader has opted to do so at his home race.

Why does Antonelli need to take a penalty?

Mercedes have generally had the car to beat for most of this year, particularly earlier in the season, but the W17 has suffered from reliability issues.

In Antonelli's case, he suffered an electrical shutdown when running in second at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix in June, which damaged one engine.

Then Mercedes discovered an issue with his engine after July's British Grand Prix, which led the team to fit Antonelli with a fourth engine at the Belgian Grand Prix three races ago, meaning he was already on the limit of the number of power units that can be used before suffering from grid penalties.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli goes past Mercedes team-mate George Russell before retiring from the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix with an engine failure

Why is Antonelli starting at the back?

F1 power units are split into different components. Had Mercedes only changed the internal combustion engine, which would be Antonelli's fifth of the season, the Italian would only have a 10-grid place penalty.

But Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says Antonelli will "take the full thing", meaning they will change other components that will take him above their respective limits, including the energy store and control electronics. They will both be worth five-grid places each, thus taking Antonelli to 20 grid places.

Once a driver has a 15-grid place penalty or more, the FIA automatically puts you at "the back of the grid", which will happen to Antonelli in Monza.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Lando Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins

Why have Mercedes chosen Monza?

Monza is known for its long straights, so overtaking is relatively easy compared to other upcoming tracks such as Madrid and Baku, which are street circuits.

At the 2021 Italian Grand Prix, Valtteri Bottas powered through from the back to the podium after an engine change, while Max Verstappen won from 14th at the 2022 Belgian Grand Prix.

"Monza is an energy-starved circuit with four overtaking zones. A driver cannot defend all of them, so a faster car should be able to make progress relatively straightforwardly," said Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin on the team's Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show.

"The primary factor is when the hardware is needed. We have lost internal combustion engines at relatively low mileage, so we know we must introduce new components by a certain point. If that falls at a circuit where starting at the back would be particularly costly, we may choose to bring the change forward."

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Italy September 4-6 Mexico Oct 30-Nov 1 Madrid September 11-13 Brazil November 6-8 Azerbaijan September 24-26 Las Vegas November 20-22 Malaysia October 2-4 Qatar November 27-29 Singapore* October 9-11 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 USA October 23-25 *denotes Sprint weekend

Currently, 12 more rounds remain of the 2026 F1 season - although that could be reduced to 11 depending on whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix take place.

Shovlin also hinted Mercedes would rather take grid penalties with Antonelli now, compared to later in the year when the title race could be closer.

"We also lead both championships, so there is logic in taking the pain now rather than adding pressure if the margins tighten later in the season," he continued.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team-mates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their Dutch Grand Prix race

What about Russell's engine situation?

Russell is in a similar position to Antonelli and will also have grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation later this season.

Sky Sports News understand that Russell will definitely not join Antonelli at the back of the grid this weekend, as Mercedes continue to assess the British driver's situation.

"We must manage the remaining events so that both cars reach the end of the season with the freshest and best-performing hardware possible," said deputy team principal Bradley Lord.

"It is a constant trade-off between the risk of running high-mileage components and the points cost of taking a grid penalty and recovering through the field."

We have a busy day's racing on Tuesday with Flat action from Brighton, Lingfield, Ripon and Wolverhampton, live on Sky Sports Racing...

5.12 Wolverhampton - Jessica seeks first win

Pierre Bonnard's half-sister Jessica will look for her first win on her third start in the second race at Wolverhampton, the Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes.

The €200,000 yearling shares the same dam as the Ballydoyle Group One winner, as well as also being a half-sister to the Group Two-placed Crepe Suzette. Of the two Amo Racing runners, it is interesting David Egan is on her as she comes here off the back of a second-placed finish at Newmarket last month which reads well as the winner, Beguiled, is entered in the Fillies' Mile.

Phalanx Nation represents Archie Watson and is entered in the Redcar Two-Year-Old Trophy in October. This filly arrives here after finishing third on both starts and the form reads very well, but she has been off since May and will need to overcome that break if she is to make it third-time lucky.

Iris Olivia took a good step forward for her first run and looks potentially progressive with Rossa Ryan in the saddle.

2.50 Lingfield - Storm Force takes on three rivals

James Doyle travels to Lingfield to take the ride on Wathnan Racing's Storm Force who takes on three rivals in the Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes.

Richard and Peter Fahey send just their third runner in five years to Lingfield as Storm Force arrives off the back of a success at Southwell. The son of Starspangledbanner travelled like a dream in the hands of Doyle and was able to come home as he pleased. Another bold show is expected under the penalty.

Best of the rest is likely to be Gold Star Gazing who is chasing a first win on his fifth start. He has a rating of 77 but could need a bit extra to beat the Fahey horse.

Blazing Gaden has raced seven times over hurdles but was behind Storm Force on his Flat debut last time out, a first attempt over six furlongs. He should know more now.

3.10 Ripon - Lexington Boom and Roman Crystal feature

The third contest on a seven-race card at Ripon sees two previous winners Lexington Boom and Roman Crystal lock horns in the 21 Engineer Regiment Sapper Nursery Handicap.

Lexington Boom drops into nursery company for the first time on his fourth career start after winning well at Beverley last month and has gone up four pounds for that success, but there is scope for plenty more to come.

Last-time-out-winner Roman Crystal has seen the track five times, scoring just the once, but there is some substance to his form, having been behind Gimcrack winner Arapaho Gold on his second start at Thirsk. He led from pillar to post last time out at Ayr, knuckling down to win nicely in the end and another bold bid is expected.

Lady Dublin comes here top-rated, having won two of her last three starts, but after a below-par performance at Newmarket, she will need to resume her progress if she is to have a say here.

The two-time US Open champion emerged from the tunnel onto the court in Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing a long, white skirt and a hooded robe featuring newspaper clippings about her.

When she removed that to reveal her black outfit, Osaka had her hair styled in cornrows, just as Iverson did when he was the NBA MVP while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers.

Sports.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.

This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka breaks the deadlock

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emi Buendia's 20-yard effort smashes the bar – but was there a foul just before?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player VAR overturns an Arsenal penalty as contact is ruled to be outside the box

Arsenal's talisman thought he had won a penalty early in the second half but Ian Maatsen's foul was ruled to be outside the box following a VAR review. It mattered not because he forced in Riccardo Calafiori's centre from close range soon afterwards.

The home side, who included debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson in their starting line-up, pushed for an equaliser but Arsenal, who brought on former Villa man Ezri Konsa late on, stayed strong to claim the win. A show of strength by the champions.

Still no shot on target for Villa Aston Villa are not only without a point from their opening two games but they are yet to register a shot on target.

The key moments from Villa Park

12 - BAR! Buendia lashes the ball against Raya's crossbar

56 - VAR! Saka denied penalty as Maatsen's foul is outside box

59 - GOAL! Calafiori's low cross is forced into the net by Saka

75 - MISS! Suzuki saves one-on-one from Havertz but he is off

Arteta hails 'massive win'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta speaking to Sky Sports:

"Really happy. A massive win. A tough place to come and earn the three points. We deserved it. A great squad performance - because when 11 wasn't enough the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to finish off the game.

"Last year we lost here in a really difficult way, with the last kick of the game. And that was still in the tummy.

"We are in the second game and it's like, 'we have to win this game!'

"We know that last year was the same. We know the level, we know how difficult it is for every team to earn points in this league, so we have to be really proud tonight."

Emery focuses on the positives

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports:

"We've lost. We competed well. We are trying to rebuild the team but a lot of positive things after the result. How we compete defensively, with the ball. We didn't create clear chances but we didn't concede clear chances. It was so equal, the match.

"Some players made their debut, fantastic. Suzuki, Jackson both very good work. The first step forward, Today is positive for the next matches.

"To lose one match is painful but after we must try to get positive things. This is the reason I am being optimistic. There are 38 matches, we played two matches and didn't achieve points but hopefully we can get better."

Arsenal's depth stands out

Tzolis has made a promising start to his Arsenal career but this was a more difficult evening for him. The response from Arteta? Bring on Eze. He helped open it up for Arsenal to win. When Villa pushed, the Arsenal boss turned to Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino to battle it out.

"Guimaraes demonstrated already with a couple of passes he's going to be something very different to what they've already got," said Gary Neville on co-commentary for Sky Sports.

"He cuts through with his passing; he always looks for that furthest forward pass. Arsenal sometimes are guilty of recycling it too much - he won't do that."

But just as significant was how robust Arsenal looked in seeing this out. As well as the physical midfield trio, Konsa came on for Cristhian Mosquera. Villa did not even manage a shot on target. Rock solid.

With different players for different situations and back-to-back wins, the Gunners have already shown why they are still the team to beat in the Premier League. And they might just have got better.

Suzuki impresses on debut

As Premier League debuts go, replacing World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez for a game against the champions Arsenal right in front of the Holte End must be among the more daunting. Suzuki acquitted himself impressively for Aston Villa.

The Japan goalkeeper failed to claim one early cross but when he tipped over a near-post header soon after, the Villa fans were chanting 'the world's number one' - a playful reference to the popular chant that was traditionally directed at Martinez at Villa Park.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville hails Ederson-esque pass from Zion Suzuki for Aston Villa

There was a little more lustre to the chant later in the first half when Suzuki pinged a pass out to George Hemmings on the left wing - arrowing the ball with extraordinary power. His distribution with both feet already looks likely to be a weapon for the team.

Suzuki did spill one fiercely struck shot in the second half but he denied Kai Havertz when one-on-one - not knowing that the offside flag would go up. Even in defeat, it was an encouraging showing by the new Villa goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Sabalenka also wins
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.

Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed from defending his title from last year.

Henman: Alcaraz got the game he wanted Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman



"If you’d have asked Alcaraz how he’d have liked this game to go, he would have signed up for a straight-sets victory, a few pressure moments, and just over two hours work.



"That is exactly what he got today. He and his team will be delighted with all aspects of this game."

"There were some doubts in the match, I'm not going to lie. Thinking about if I would last the match, best of five, playing four or five sets," said Alcaraz, who will play Portugal's Jaime Faria in the next round.

"I had a little bit of doubt, but I tried to forget everything and focus on the things I needed to improve. I thought about what would happen in the match and physically I felt really well."

Watched on by rapper Travis Scott, who helped design Alcaraz's brown outfit for the US Open, there was plenty of attention on the seven-time Grand Slam champion's serve and groundstroke speed, given he had not played competitive singles for over four months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz reflected on his US Open round one win. against Roman Safiullin

He needed to save two break points from Safiullin in his opening three service games before breaking himself in the eighth game which proved enough to claim the opening set.

Alcaraz was broken at the start of the second set but broke back immediately and upped his intensity to break in the eighth game again and go on to win the second set.

After an early break in the third set, Alcaraz never came under threat on his serve and continued to move well while maintaining a high level on both wins to see off the tricky Russian.

One of the biggest threats in Alcaraz's half was Arthur Fils, after he won the Cincinnati Open title last week, but he was knocked out of the tournament by Stefanos Tsitsipas in a 4-6 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 6-4 defeat.

Sabalenka overcomes Osorio test

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Aryna Sabalenka and Camila Osorio

Like Alcaraz, Aryna Sabalenka started her US Open title with a straight-sets win as she beat Colombia's Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4.

Sabalenka is bidding to become the first player to win three consecutive US Open titles since Serena Williams in 2014 and was put under serious pressure by Osorio in the second set.

"Camila is a tough opponent but I was ready to do whatever it takes to get the win," she told Sky Sports Tennis.

"I really enjoyed the atmosphere and support. A fun and tough match but happy to get through in straight sets."

Sabalenka's form has been questioned after losing in the last 16 in her last three tournaments - Wimbledon, the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open.

It means she could lose her status as world No 1 for the first time since October 2024 with Elena Rybakina, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula all having the chance to knock Sabalenka off her perch.

But Sabalenka's best surface is the hard court, having won her four Grand Slam titles on hard, and her raw power will always make the Belarusian difficult to beat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka hits back at critics, saying she is tired of the negativity surrounding her with everything she does both on and off the court

Elsewhere, Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova will be looking for another big run and she got off to a great start by beating Austria's Sinja Karus 6-3 6-0.

Last year's US Open runner-up Amanda Anisimova defeated compatriot Ashlyn Krueger 6-1 6-3 and was joined by three more victorious Americans in the women's draw on Monday as Emma Navarro, Taylor Townsend and Cate McNally also won.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How many previous US Open winners could you name in 20 seconds?

Brits Dart and Fearnley fight back to progress; Wendelken out

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Jacob Fearnley and Martin Landaluce

Britain's Harriet Dart and Jacob Fearnley both fought back from losing positions to reach the second round of the US Open.

Dart was a set and a break down before roaring back to a 3-6 6-3 6-2 win over American Peyton Stearns.

Her coach and Sky Sports Tennis pundit Marion Bartoli said: "I'm really pleased for her. Such a great effort and mentally it's so hard to come back but she fought so hard. It's absolutely brilliant."

That was followed by a superb win for Jacob Fearnley after he beat Spain's Martin Landaluce 4-6 6-2 4-6 7-5 6-3.

Landaluce served for the match in the fourth set but Fearnley won three games in a row to take the match to a deciding set and continued that momentum in the fifth.

Despite missing a routine smash to win the match, Fearnley kept his composure and ensured he made the second round at Flushing Meadows for a second successive year.

Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka hit back at her critics, saying "haters can go and get on with their own lives" after she made a winning start in her quest for a ‌third successive US Open title.

Sabalenka is attempting to regain her usual dominance after a frustrating last six months, ​having failed to reach a final since she completed the Sunshine Double in March, but she made a confident start to her quest for a ‌rare 'three-peat' at the year's final major.

The world No 1 launched 32 winners to defeat Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4 in the first match of the day ‌on Arthur Ashe Stadium to set up a meeting with Russia's Polina Iatcenko in the second round.

Sports.title: Manchester City gazump Spurs over Iliman Ndiaye and eye Enzo Fernández deal
Sports.content:
Manchester City are poised to bolster their attack by buying Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye for up to £65m and have opened talks with Chelsea over a deal to sign Enzo Fernández.

City’s hijack of Tottenham’s deal for Ndiaye came after their attempts to sign Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo broke down. The Senegal international is poised to undergo a medical after a fee of £60m plus £5m in add-ons was agreed with Everton, who have little time to find a replacement for one of their most important players before the transfer window shuts on Tuesday night.

It had seemed that Ndiaye would move to Spurs after they agreed a deal in principle with Everton on Sunday. Richarlison was poised to move in the opposite direction but that transfer stalled on Monday. Richarlison released an emotional statement on social media and said that he would not allow his future to be decided for him. The Brazilian is cool on a move to Everton and is expected to stay at Spurs.

City registered their interest in Ndiaye last week and moved in after Liverpool pulled out of an £85m deal for Gakpo. Spurs have moved on and agreed to sign Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea.

The Ukraine winger, who is free to play again after his doping ban was resolved this summer, played for Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk and favoured a reunion with the Tottenham manager after Leeds and Brentford also contacted Chelsea about him.

Spurs have also agreed a deal to sign Chelsea’s defender Tosin Adarabioyo on a permanent deal.

Chelsea are poised for a busy end to the window and have finally been contacted by City about Fernández. The Argentina midfielder wants to leave and has his heart set on a move to City. Fernández has a close relationship with City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who left Chelsea this year.

Chelsea set a price of £120m for Fernández this summer and may push for a higher fee with the deadline drawing close. Another consideration for the Stamford Bridge club as they face up to losing one of their biggest players is the need to improve their squad.
