World.title: Liberia: UMC Bishop Declares Africa “New Epicenter Of Faith” At Thanksgiving Service In Monrovia
World.content:
Monrovia, August 30, 2026 – The preacher at the Thanksgiving Service in Monrovia ahead of 2026 Africa College of Bishops Meeting has called on the global church to “enlarge its tent” and prepare for unprecedented growth, declaring Africa the new epicenter of Christianity.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The service, held at the historic First United Methodist Church and hosted by the Liberia Episcopal Area, set the pace for the opening of the 2026 Africa College of Bishops Meeting. At the Thanksgiving Service, Bishops, clergies, and lay leaders from across the continent and the U.S. gathered under the theme drawn from Isaiah 54:2: “Enlarge the place of your tent.”

Delivering the sermon, Bishop L. Jonathan Holston of the Alabama-West Florida Episcopal Area of the United States Southeastern Jurisdiction, cautioned the congregation that God is demanding “a new way of stretching and a new way of doing things.”

“We are witnessing a monumental shift in the landscape of global Christianity. Africa is emerging as a new epicenter of the faith,” Bishop Holston declared.

“This is a season of spiritual preparation and transition. While the center of influence has shifted, it brings with it a sacred responsibility: To develop leaders; to engage our communities and to make room for what God is doing next.”

A Call To Expand And Lead Courageously

Preaching from Isaiah 54:2, Bishop Holston urged Methodists and the Christian community to move beyond their comfort zones and traditional thinking.

“God is calling us to expand – spiritually and structurally. True progress is not about changing titles. It’s about changing hearts. To fulfill this divine mandate, we must: Love boldly. Serve joyfully. Lead courageously.”

He challenged the church to reach “people you have never seen before, and speak to people you have never spoken to before,” including younger generations and those divided by politics.

“It’s time to stretch beyond rigid traditions and political divisions. It’s time to create space for God to work through us,” Bishop Holston stated, adding: “The world needs our witness. God is calling us forward, not backward. This is the moment to go.”

The Bishop acknowledged current challenges confronting the world maintained that no situation should ever deter Christians from advancing further.

“We are living in a time of political uncertainty and inflation, but we must be ready to go forth. Do not hold back.”

“Do not be afraid. The most impactful work of the Church is still ahead of us. This is a word of expansion. Prepare yourself. Enlarge your capacity. Welcome the larger, more inclusive future God is bringing,” the renowned US-based Methodist Church Bishop added.

The service was climaxed with prayers for the bishops, the Liberia Episcopal Area, and for the United Methodist Church worldwide as well as Christians across the globe.

Liberia Hosts Continental Gathering

The Thanksgiving Service served as both worship and preparation for the week-long Africa College of Bishops Meeting hosted by the Liberia Episcopal Area. The meeting, which will be hosted at the Farmington Hotel Town in Unification Town, Margibi County, will focus on leadership development, evangelism strategies, and the church’s role in addressing social issues across Africa.

“Do not be afraid. The most impactful work of the Church is still ahead of us. This is a word of expansion. Prepare yourself. Enlarge your capacity. Welcome the larger, more inclusive future God is bringing.”

The service concluded with prayers for the bishops, the Liberia Episcopal Area, and for the United Methodist Church worldwide.

World.title: Jackson F. Doe Hospital Expansion Signals Liberia’s Push to Decentralize Specialized Healthcare
World.content:
TAPPITA, Nimba County — The Government of Liberia is advancing plans to expand specialized healthcare services outside Monrovia with a major upgrade of the Jackson F. Doe Memorial Regional Referral Hospital in Tappita, Nimba County.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The government has dedicated newly constructed housing for healthcare workers and broken ground for a new emergency room, intensive care unit (ICU), and three additional duplexes for hospital staff.

The projects form part of an ambitious plan to transform Jackson F. Doe into a major regional referral center and, eventually, Liberia’s second national referral hospital.

Speaking at the ceremony over the weekend, Deputy Minister for Fiscal Affairs Anthony G. Myers, who represented Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung and Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, said the investment demonstrates the government’s commitment to extending critical public services beyond Monrovia.

“Strengthening healthcare infrastructure outside Monrovia is fundamental to inclusive national development,” Myers said, noting that Jackson F. Doe Hospital has been designated a priority Public Sector Investment Program (PSIP) project.

US$44.4 Million Invested Since 2010

According to Myers, Jackson F. Doe Hospital was incorporated into Liberia’s national budget in 2010, and the government has since invested approximately US$44.4 million in the facility.

Of that amount, about US$3.9 million was allocated during the 2026 fiscal year, he said.

Myers warned, however, that additional resources will be required as the hospital’s catchment area expands and improved road connectivity makes Tappita more accessible to patients from Nimba and neighboring counties.

Focus on Emergency and Critical Care

A major component of the latest expansion is the construction of a new emergency room and intensive care unit, facilities expected to strengthen the hospital’s capacity to treat life-threatening illnesses, severe injuries and other medical emergencies.

Myers said the investment is about more than constructing physical infrastructure.

“When a patient arrives with a life-threatening condition, the quality and speed of emergency care can determine the outcome,” he said.

The government expects improved emergency and specialist services at Jackson F. Doe to reduce pressure on referral hospitals in Monrovia by allowing more patients from southeastern and central Liberia to access advanced treatment closer to home.

Staff Housing Targets Retention Challenges

The staff housing component is intended to address another persistent challenge facing regional healthcare facilities: the recruitment and retention of qualified health professionals.

Myers said adequate accommodation for doctors, nurses, specialists and other healthcare workers is critical to retaining skilled personnel and ensuring continuity of services at the hospital.

He also commended the hospital’s financial management, noting that its 2025 budget execution rate exceeded the health sector average of 97 percent.

However, he acknowledged growing pressure on health financing as some external sources of funding decline.

Myers said the government is responding by reallocating resources within the national budget to protect essential health services.

Part of Boakai’s ARREST Agenda

The Jackson F. Doe expansion is being implemented under President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development and is listed as a priority PSIP project.

For a country where advanced medical services remain heavily concentrated in Monrovia, the expansion could represent a significant step toward decentralizing healthcare and bringing specialized treatment closer to patients in the counties.

The government says the investment is part of a broader, long-term strategy to strengthen Liberia’s national referral system and expand access to specialized and life-saving medical care outside the capital.

Myers Honored in Nimba

During the visit, chiefs and elders of Nimba District Six honored Deputy Minister Myers for what they described as his contribution to the development of the region.

The ceremony brought together Nimba County Senator Nya D. Twayen Jr.; Nimba District Six Representative Dorwohn Twain Gleekia; Deputy Health Minister for Research, Policy and Monitoring & Evaluation Atty. Malayah Tamba Chieyoe; Deputy Director General for Administration at the Liberia Civil Aviation Authority Stephen R. Johnson; hospital administrators; and local government officials.

World.title: Liberia: Cummings Demands Speedy, Fair Trial for Howard-Taylor, Accuses Government of ‘Selective Justice’
World.content:
Monrovia – Political Leader of the Alternative National Congress, Alexander Benedict Cummings, has called on the Government of Liberia to ensure a speedy and fair trial for former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor, who remains incarcerated at the Monrovia Central Prison over allegations linked to the country’s ongoing narcotics investigation.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

Cummings made the call Sunday after visiting Howard-Taylor at the prison, commonly known as “South Beach,” where she is being held in connection with the drug case.

Speaking to reporters after the visit, Cummings accused the government of applying justice selectively and warned that Liberia risks becoming a “narco-state” if authorities fail to prosecute all individuals implicated in the narcotics trade, regardless of their political status.

Cummings said his visit was personal but acknowledged that it carried a broader political message.

“I came this afternoon to visit the former Vice President, Jewel Howard-Taylor. The former Vice President is a friend; I call her my ‘small sister.’ I came to empathize with her and check on her circumstantial situation,” he said.

Cummings declined to disclose details of his private conversation with Howard-Taylor but said she feels aggrieved and maintains that authorities do not have sufficient evidence against her.

“That conversation was private between her and me. She obviously feels aggrieved. She feels they have no evidence, etc., but I will say no more than this,” he said.

Cummings Calls for Speedy Justice

The ANC political leader outlined what he described as key principles that should guide the government’s handling of the narcotics investigation, with a speedy trial among his principal demands.

“One is, of course, the legal piece of it: the innocent are presumed innocent until proven guilty. There is a presumption of innocence, and the evidence should be followed wherever it leads,” Cummings said.

“But justice needs to be speedy. It needs to be speedy, and justice should not be selective. It appears that justice is being selectively prescribed,” he added.

Cummings said Liberia’s narcotics problem has become increasingly serious under the current administration and called for the prosecution and arrest of all persons implicated in the drug trade.

“This narcotic issue is a serious problem for our country. Our country appears to be becoming a narco-state, and it is happening now under this government’s watch,” he said.

“We want to see prosecution. We want to see arrests of current officials because it is happening now.”

Demands Independent Investigation

Cummings also renewed his call for an independent investigation into the narcotics allegations, citing comments attributed to the Inspector General of Police that senior government officials were allegedly implicated.

“The Inspector General of Police, in his press conference, said there were big shots, big heads in this government who were implicated. We want to know who they are because otherwise the process seems unjust. It seems selective,” Cummings said.

He argued that an independent process would help establish the facts and ensure that the law is applied equally to current and former officials.

ANC Vows to Keep Pressure on Government

Cummings said the ANC would continue to hold the government accountable beyond the ongoing narcotics investigation, citing corruption, injustice and other governance concerns.

“The next step of the party is to keep reminding the government of ills in society, including corruption, injustices, violence and drugs,” he said.

“We want this narco-state situation to be curtailed. We want the government to go after corruption. You know, we wrote a letter on this whole Foya construction in Lofa. We haven’t gotten a response. We will be speaking on that again.”

Cummings also confirmed that he had followed through on an earlier commitment to engage international partners over Liberia’s narcotics crisis.

“I said I would speak to international partners to get involved, and I did do that. I just hope this government does the right thing. It’s not about taking sides here or there. It’s about following the evidence, but applying it to everybody,” he said.

While expressing sympathy for Howard-Taylor, Cummings stopped short of declaring her innocent, instead insisting that the government should present whatever evidence it has against her.

“It is not my impression that the person, the woman I know, will be involved in what is being alleged. But again, let’s see the evidence. That’s why they need to do it quickly, speedily, and provide whatever evidence they have,” he said.

The ANC said it will continue to demand speedy trials and justice for everyone incarcerated in connection with the narcotics investigation, including the former Vice President.

World.title: Liberia: Nimba Elders Back Boakai’s Drug Fight, Warn Illicit Drugs Threaten Liberia’s Future
World.content:
Monrovia — The Nimba Council of Elders has thrown its support behind the government’s ongoing crackdown on illicit drugs, commending President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and his administration for what it described as the political will and determination to confront the growing drug menace in Liberia.

In a press release dated August 21, the Council said the government should remain resolute in detecting illegal drug activities, holding perpetrators accountable and ensuring that the law takes its course, regardless of the status or influence of those involved.

The Elders acknowledged that no government can completely prevent individuals with criminal intentions from attempting to smuggle illegal substances into the country, but said the true test of leadership lies in the willingness to uncover such activities and prosecute those responsible.

The Council urged the government to pursue the fight against illicit drugs “without fear or favor,” regardless of political affiliation, social status, influence or personal connections.

“Drugs know no tribe, political party, religion or social status. Their consequences reach every community, destroy the lives of our young people, weaken families and threaten the future of our nation,” the Council stated.

The statement comes amid heightened national concern over Liberia’s escalating drug crisis and recent major narcotics seizures that have triggered calls for stronger law enforcement and accountability.

The Nimba elders also stressed that the responsibility for combating illicit drugs cannot rest solely with the government.

They called on traditional and religious leaders, parents, young people, civil society organizations, communities and citizens across Liberia to actively participate in efforts to prevent drug abuse and trafficking.

“As elders, we have a responsibility not only to the present generation but also to those yet unborn. We must not leave to our children a country overwhelmed by a problem we had the opportunity and responsibility to confront,” the Council emphasized.

The Council further called for stronger measures in drug prevention, law enforcement, prosecution, treatment and rehabilitation, arguing that a comprehensive national response is needed to effectively address the problem.

The Elders reaffirmed their support for what they described as every lawful and genuine effort to combat illicit drugs, while urging all Liberians to unite behind efforts aimed at protecting young people and safeguarding the country’s future.

World.title: Baby Born With Teeth: How Mundubile’s Alliance Shook HH But Couldn’t Bite!
World.content:
By Prince Bill M. Kaping’a

Part 1

After suffering a shock defeat in the August 2021 general elections, Lungu abruptly announced his retirement from active politics. However, he soon reversed that decision and sought to reclaim leadership of the party.

Like any party recovering from an electoral loss, the PF was expected to hold a convention, usher in new leaders, and focus on rebuilding. That did not happen. Instead, the party inflicted injuries on itself that caused it to hemorrhage, leading to a split into several factions.

The crisis began with a controversial convention in October 2023 that installed Miles Sampa as party leader. A High Court ruling in March 2024 reaffirmed Sampa as PF president for the 2023-2028 term.

Soon after, the Robert Chabinga faction emerged. It was recognised by the Registrar of Societies and in Parliament, positioned itself as a reformist group, and aligned with the ruling UPND.

Once Lungu had gathered enough courage, he declared his return to politics and effectively took over what was left of the former ruling party.

He remained in the background while Given Lubinda held the fort as Acting President, with the firebrand Raphael Nakacinda serving as Secretary General. The group presented itself as the bridge between the Lungu era and the future. It immediately began pushing for an Extraordinary Convention to elect new leaders, even as it fought running legal battles with the Chabinga camp in court.

Following the Constitutional Court’s decision to disqualify Lungu from contesting the 2026 general elections — and of course his eventual passing — the faction eased Lubinda out of leadership and moved to crown Brian Mundubile, the Mporokoso MP, as its new leader.

Positioning itself as election-ready, the group embarked on serious mobilization, particularly on the Copperbelt and in Lusaka. Sensing that the PF would not appear on the ballot papers, Mundubile opted to contest under a little-known political party, the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity — NRPUP. He would eventually enter into a marriage of convenience with several small political parties and form the Tonse Alliance.

In no time, prominent Lusaka lawyer Makebi Zulu, who had assumed the role of the Lungu family spokesperson after Lungu’s death, joined the fray and launched his own Resolute Party. It became the anchor of the PF Pamodzi Alliance.

Before long, Mundubile and Makebi formed an alliance that would later prove to be “a baby born with teeth.” Almost overnight, the partnership turned the political landscape upside down, drawing massive crowds to rallies and record followings on social media platforms.

One thing was clear: although PF had lost the 2021 general elections, its support base had remained intact and was eager to reclaim power by all means.

Frustrated with Hichilema over load shedding, the soaring price of the staple food mealie-meal, and the cost of fuel, the electorate along the line of rail seemed to be drawn to what Mundubile was offering.

World.title: M’membe Lays Out Sweeping Reform Agenda Ahead of Hichilema’s Second-Term Inauguration
World.content:
On the eve of President Hakainde Hichilema’s inauguration for a second term, Socialist Party president Fred M’membe released a wide-ranging policy manifesto calling for structural reforms across government, mining, taxation, and urban planning, framing Zambia’s economic and social system as afflicted by what he termed “high viscosity syndrome” — a condition in which upward mobility is blocked, merit is undermined by patronage networks, and public resources are consumed by an oversized state apparatus.

In a post on his Facebook page, M’membe urged the incoming administration to move decisively from what he described as bureaucratic consumption toward grassroots wealth creation, presenting the proposals as a “loyal opposition” manifesto for the new term.

Cutting the size of government

M’membe called for parliamentary and local council business to move to a fully digital model, arguing this would eliminate the recurring cost of centralized physical sessions in Lusaka and in council chambers nationwide. Under his proposal, members of Parliament and ward councillors would work from constituency-based digital hubs, attending live virtual legislative sessions while being required to spend a statutory minimum number of days each year physically present in their constituencies, except during declared national emergencies.

The manifesto also calls for the permanent abolition of political advisor positions across government ministries and of the office of District Commissioner, with local district administration handled instead by professional, merit-based civil servants. It proposes consolidating Cabinet into a smaller, non-duplicative executive team, with Permanent Secretary appointments made strictly on technocratic grounds and governed by performance-based delivery contracts. M’membe additionally proposed eliminating all Deputy High Commissioner and Deputy Ambassador posts across Zambia’s foreign missions, saying missions should be staffed leanly and focused on trade and commercial diplomacy.

Settling 500,000 youths on productive land

M’membe proposed that savings from downsizing government be redirected into large-scale youth settlement and vocational programs rather than general spending. The plan calls for settling 500,000 trained youths as commercial producers on state-allocated agricultural land across all provinces, with settlement packages that go beyond land titles to include mechanized land preparation, solar-powered boreholes, starter seed and input packs, and training in commercial crop production, poultry, aquaculture, and horticulture.

A parallel vocational track would provide young bricklayers, mechanics, plumbers, and electricians with professional toolkits, equipment-leasing credit lines, and guaranteed access to local public maintenance contracts. M’membe argued this would expand the domestic tax base, strengthen food security, and connect GDP growth more directly to household incomes.

Expanding state equity in mining

On the mining sector, M’membe’s manifesto calls not for privatization but for an expanded state ownership stake. It proposes requiring a minimum 51% equity stake for ZCCM-IH in all new mining licenses, with existing mines offered a 30% state equity option. Dividends from these holdings would flow into a proposed Copper Revenue Stabilisation Fund, which the manifesto models on Chile’s FEES fund and Botswana’s Pula Fund.

The plan also calls for a dedicated Transfer Pricing Enforcement Unit, supported by GPS-enabled monitoring of mineral exports and mandatory quarterly revenue reporting, which M’membe said would close loopholes that have allowed mineral wealth to leave the country undertaxed.

Tax changes

The manifesto calls for the immediate repeal of taxes on mobile money transactions, arguing they function as a barrier to financial inclusion for micro-merchants, market traders, and rural households, and proposes shifting that tax burden onto service providers instead of users. It also calls for widened Pay-As-You-Earn tax brackets to increase disposable household income.

Separately, the plan proposes a new wealth tax targeting luxury real estate, offshore assets, and unproductive domestic capital, along with an escalating land holdings tax on any landholding above 200 hectares. Under the proposal, that land tax would be waived only if the titleholder can show active commercial use of the land through filed turnover tax, income tax, and VAT returns.

A cess on commercial frontage properties

M’membe’s manifesto describes a spatial divide in Zambian cities, where malls, office parks, and commercial plazas sit along main roads while the compounds directly behind them lack paved roads, drainage, water, and sanitation. To address this, it proposes a mandatory Municipal Community Cess applied nationwide to commercial properties on primary and secondary road frontages, including retail malls, corporate offices, fuel stations, banks, distribution yards, and private health facilities.

City, municipal, and town councils would set the rating schedules based on local valuation rolls, traffic volume, and commercial footprint. By law, all cess revenue would be ring-fenced into a Compound Infrastructure and Human Development Fund, barred from covering council salaries or general administrative costs, and instead used to pave internal compound roads, install stormwater drainage, extend treated water networks, install street lighting, build solar-powered digital learning hubs, and construct electrified market stalls for informal traders.

Mining sector labor and environmental provisions

The manifesto proposes a statutory windfall profit-sharing mechanism requiring mining companies to distribute a set percentage of excess revenue to mine workers during periods of high global metal prices, along with mandatory inflation-indexed hazardous duty allowances for underground and high-risk personnel. It also calls for higher, differentiated road tolls on mining transport fleets to offset road wear caused by heavy mineral haulage, which M’membe said currently falls on regular motorists.

On the environment, the plan calls for mining houses to pay a fixed statutory charge per metric tonne of ore extracted — or a set percentage of gross export value — into an independently audited Environmental Remediation and Resettlement Sinking Fund. It calls for real-time, progressive ecological rehabilitation of land, rivers, and vegetation as mining advances, rather than remediation deferred until mine closure, and for immediate resettlement of communities living in industrial pollution zones, with new housing, water access, and soil detoxification. The manifesto further proposes giving the state a statutory first lien over mining companies’ physical assets, processing plants, and export receivables until independent auditors certify environmental reclamation is complete.

M’membe’s framing

M’membe said maintaining the current system — protecting redundant offices, insulating politically connected insiders, and taxing the poor while rewarding speculators — would not break what he called Zambia’s cycle of generational poverty. He said the combined package of measures was intended to “dissolve systemic friction and unleash the latent energy, talent, and enterprise of every Zambian.”

— Based on a policy manifesto released by Fred M’membe, President of the Socialist Party of Zambia.

World.title: North Chief hails HH leadership
World.content:
Chief Mwamba of the Mambwe people of Mbala district has expressed optimism that President Hakainde Hichilema’s administration will continue to roll-out development, following his re-election in the August 13, general elections.

The traditional leader says he remains hopeful that the government will accelerate development in Mbala district, particularly in the road sector.

Chief Mwamba cited the road leading to the Zombe border, as well as the road connecting Kawimbe through Mwamba chiefdom to Kaka, as some of the developmental projects that need urgent attention.

He said improved road infrastructure will boost economic activities and make it easier for people in the area to access markets and essential services.

Chief Mwamba said this in an interview with the media in Mbala today.

“Improved roads will not only enhance connectivity, but will also open up opportunities for our people to participate more actively in economic activities,” Chief Mwamba said.

The traditional leader has also appealed to UPND Member of Parliament for Saise, Remmy Sikazwe, to help facilitate the completion of his palace.

World.title: Serenje Chief calls for illegal mining end
World.content:
Senior Chief Muchinda of the Lala people of Serenje district has called on the government to curb illegal mining in the area, which he says endangers the lives of the youths in his chiefdom.

Chief Muchinda notes that illegal mining activities pose a threat, saying those engaged, continue to conduct mining activities without taking safety precautions.

The traditional leader made these remarks when Serenje District Commissioner Ellen Miselo, who is on a familiarisation tour of the district, paid a courtesy call on him.

He explained that illegal mining activities have become prevalent in his area, with young people being employed without proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), thereby endangering their lives.

“We need to work together to fight illegal mining to safeguard the lives of our children. We need to deal with criminals, illegal miners and those selling land illegally, in order to preserve our land,” he said.

And Senior Chief Muchinda said most mining companies operating in his area are doing so illegally, stating that they are not undertaking Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programmes in the chiefdom.

He urged the government to regulate the working conditions of mine workers and ensure that they are provided with the necessary protective and working equipment.

Meanwhile, Serenje District Commissioner Ellen Mibenge commended the traditional leader for preserving trees in his chiefdom and assured him of the government’s support in fostering development in the district.

She said her office will ensure that investors comply with the law so that local people will benefit from their investments.

World.title: UPND petitions parley seats in Muchinga
World.content:
The United Party for National Development (UPND) has petitioned for two parliamentary seats in the Chinsali High Court in Muchinga Province.

The seats are the Chinsali Central seat in Chinsali District where UPND candidate, Christopher Chiponde has petitioned the election of Chanda Mwansa of the National Restoration Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP).

The other is the Shiwangandu seat in Shiwangandu district where a UPND supporter and voter, Victor Beleshi has petitioned the election of Stephen Kampyongo of the NRPUP.

According to records obtained by the media at the Chinsali High Court, Mr Chiponde is seeking the court to nullify the results of the parliamentary election.

Mr Chiponde said the election was marred with shockingly widespread illegalities and violence against persons and property.

He cited other grounds to warrant the nullification of the results as alleged intimidation, corruption, procedural breaches and other misconduct during the election that declared Mr Mwansa.

The petitioner further alleged that there was widespread non- compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Process Act no. 35 of 2016 stating that this affected the outcome of the elections.

Mr Chiponde has further cited Mr Mwansa who was declared winner as the first respondent, while the Electoral Commission of Zambia as the second respondent.

And in Shiwang’andu Constituency, Victor Beleshi a voter who is also a member of the United Party for National Development (UPND) has petitioned for the parliamentary seat.

The Petitioner is seeking recourse against the respondent Stephen Kampyongo Member of Parliament elect in Shiwangandu Constituency and wants the results be declared null and void.

Mr Beleshi stated that NRPUP members at various polling stations were allowed to vote for more than two people and spent long periods of time inside the polling stations.

The other grounds have been cited are that at some polling stations, the respondent and his agents were giving money to the electorates and evidence abounds in this area.

The NRPUP scooped both the Chinsali Central seat and the Shiwangandu parliamentary seat during the August 13th general election.

NRPUP candidate Chanda Mwansa obtained 11254 votes against Christopher Chiponde of the UPND who got 4430 votes.

In the Shiwangandu, Stephen Kampyongo got 11,536 votes against Robert Kapeya of the UPND who got 9941 votes.

Both seats were petitioned on Friday, August 28th, 2026.

World.title: We’ll be back for the title – Mwila
World.content:
ZESCO Ndola Girls Head Coach Florence Mwila has described Saturday’s 2-1 defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns in the CAF Women’s Champions League COSAFA Qualifier final as “not part of the plan” but says her team will return stronger.

It was déjà vu for the Zambian champions, who were losing finalists for the second year running after conceding a controversial late penalty in Botswana.

“I think we started on a very slow note, but the positive thing is that the girls pushed, equalized,” Mwila said.

“Obviously they were so much under pressure, so we conceded that penalty which really put us down,” she said.

Despite the heartbreak, Mwila said there were positives to take from the tournament. ZESCO topped Group A with 9 points from 3 wins and beat *Silver Strikers 2-1 to reach the final.

“We have picked up positives from here like the commitment and the fighting spirit from the players, “she said.

“We have a task to defend the championship back home. We will improve in the grey areas as a team so that when we come back we will come back for the title.”

With the win, Mamelodi Sundowns will represent the COSAFA region at the CAF Women’s Champions League continental finals.

World.title: Government calls for stronger HAI surveillance
World.content:
Government has called for stronger and sustainable Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) surveillance systems across Africa to improve patient safety and strengthen the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

Ministry of Health Permanent Secretary for Technical Services, Kennedy Lishimpi, says healthcare-associated infection surveillance should be integrated into routine national surveillance and quality of care systems, rather than remain a stand-alone activity dependent on external support.

Dr Lishimpi was speaking in Lusaka today, when he officiated at the Multi-Country Training of Trainers on Healthcare-Associated Infection Surveillance (HAIs), which has brought together national Infection Prevention and Control and Antimicrobial Resistance focal persons, from 13 African Union Member States.

He said reliable surveillance is critical in helping health facilities identify priority infections, detect outbreaks early, determine the organisms involved and link laboratory and clinical data to appropriate infection prevention and control measures.

“Healthcare-associated infections are not merely statistics,” Dr. Lishimpi said, noting that such infections can delay patient recovery, increase risks to newborns and health workers as well as impose additional costs on families and health systems.

He said the surveillance of HAIs is also central to addressing antimicrobial resistance because infections acquired during healthcare often result in additional or prolonged antimicrobial treatment, while resistant organisms make infections more difficult and costly to manage.

He called for the cascading of training to subnational and facility levels and the regular analysis and sharing of surveillance data with health workers and managers to support decision-making.

Dr Lishimpi said sustainable HAIs surveillance requires trained personnel, reliable laboratories, appropriate digital and paper-based tools, adequate water, sanitation and hygiene infrastructure as well as domestic financing.

He also stressed the importance of regional collaboration and peer learning in helping African countries adopt common standards and strengthen their surveillance systems.

He disclosed that the World Health Organisation estimates that about 15 in every 100 patients in acute-care hospitals in low and middle-income countries acquire at least one healthcare-associated infection.

And Africa CDC Director General Jean Kaseya in a speech read for him by Africa CDC Regional Director Peter Kumpalume, called for stronger measures to prevent hospital-acquired infections.

Dr Kaseya Africa CDC said HAIs are among the most frequent adverse events occurring in hospitals, with a significant proportion being preventable through stronger infection prevention and control systems.

He noted that HAIs not only put patients at risk but also place an additional burden on health systems through increased hospital bed occupancy, medicine use and pressure on doctors, nurses and laboratory personnel.

He also said infection prevention and control should be institutionalised as a permanent component of clinical care.

Dr Kaseya reaffirmed Africa CDCs commitment to supporting member states in strengthening infection prevention and control.

World.title: Hero stadium turf protector Installed
World.content:
The Ministry of Youth, Sport, and Arts has confirmed the installation of the turf protector at the Presidential Inauguration venue, Heroes Stadium.

The Ministry’s Principal Public Relations Officer, Bobby Ng’andu, highlighted that the protector is intended to safeguard and extend the lifespan of the turf, which was purchased earlier at a cost of $1.4 million.

He made these remarks in an interview the media during the installation earlier this morning.

Mr Ng’andu has since urged members of the public scheduled to attend the inauguration tomorrow to take ownership by refraining from vandalising any property at the venue.

“I can safely confirm today that the turf protector is in place, and people are working around the clock to ensure everything is in order,” he said.

He added that the turf came at a significant cost and must be protected to ensure its durability, noting that there are other future activities planned for the stadium beyond tomorrow’s inauguration.

Mr Ng’andu also emphasised that tomorrow is a big day for the country, and people should not only enjoy the inauguration but also safeguard the infrastructure jealously.

He further commended other line ministries and members of the organising committee for working in unison towards tomorrow’s event.

The venue is now ready for the presidential inauguration ceremony for President-elect Hakainde Hichilema.

World.title: South Africa: Limpopo Village Cut Off as Bridge Collapses - South African News Briefs - September 1, 2026
World.content:
Limpopo Village Cut Off After Makeshift Bridge Collapses

The community of Mafarafara village in Limpopo has once again been cut off from a nearby clinic after a makeshift bridge across the Tubatse River collapsed following recent heavy rains, reports EWN. The bridge, built from wooden logs, sticks and corrugated iron sheets, provided a vital but unsafe link between remote villages. Residents must now either swim across the swollen river or pay more than R100 for transport to and from the clinic.



Hawks Officer Questioned Over R3 Million Cash Deposits

The Madlanga Commission has questioned KwaZulu-Natal Hawks Lieutenant-Colonel Deenadayalan Govender over more than R3 million in cash deposits made into his bank accounts between August 2022 and December 2023, reports SABC News. The commission said that the deposits far exceeded his monthly take-home salary. He is being investigated to determine whether the movement of the funds could indicate possible money laundering. Govender has also faced questions about his relationships with tow-truck businessman Clive Naicker and convicted drug dealer Timmy Marimuthu.

Cape Town Signs Cheaper Solar Power Deals

Cape Town has signed two solar power purchase agreements that will add 70 megawatts of electricity from plants in Atlantis and Philippi to the city's grid at prices below Eskom's tariffs, reports EWN. The city said that the future price increases will be linked to inflation rather than Eskom's tariff hikes. This might potentially help to limit electricity costs for residents. Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis said the 20-year contracts are expected to provide R8 billion worth of electricity and reduce the city's reliance on Eskom.
